walks.title: Add a class to a group

steps.say: **Add a class** creates a class under this group before anyone is teaching it yet — useful for setting a term up in advance.
Type the class name, then choose the course it will learn. A paid language your group has no cover for is refused when you tap Add, and the message says so.
**Add** creates it. No teacher is needed yet — the class sits under the group waiting, and you can put a teacher on it whenever you're ready.
steps.terminal: That's adding a class ahead of staffing it. This tour added nobody and nothing; only your own tap does.

walks.title: Add a school to your programme

steps.say: **+ Add school** creates a new school inside your programme. It exists the moment you name it, already attached to your group, with its admin and teacher links ready to hand over.

Type the school's name, tap **Create school**, then copy its Admin and Teacher links to send to whoever runs it. Both links stay on the school's own row afterwards, so you can fetch them again any time.
steps.terminal: That's a new school made — no separate onboarding step to remember.

walks.title: Add a student to a class

steps.say: On the class's own page, tap **Invite students**.
Type the student's name. Add their email if you want us to send it, or leave it blank and you get a link to hand over yourself — then submit, and repeat for the next student.
steps.terminal: One student at a time, on purpose — the link is theirs alone and carries the class with it. The Students page's + Invite students button brings you here for exactly this reason.

walks.title: Add students to a class

steps.say: Above the roster, tap **Add students** — for a pupil already in your school who has changed set or landed in the wrong class.
Type a few letters of their name to narrow the list, then tap the pupil — they appear on the roster straight away. Add as many as you need, then tap Done.
steps.terminal: Adding doesn't take them out of any other class — a pupil can be in more than one, one for each course they're doing. A pupil with no account at all needs the class link in Invite students instead.

walks.title: Add a teacher by name

steps.say: Tap **Add by name** when you know exactly who is joining but can't rely on email reaching them.

Type their name and tap **Create code**. That mints their access code on the spot — read it out, write it down, or paste it wherever you already reach them. They use it once at saysomethingin.app/join.
steps.terminal: They appear on your list straight away under Not yet given classes, so you can tick their classes before they've even signed in.

walks.title: Choose what a class learns

steps.say: Every class carries one course — it decides what the class practises and what students hear the moment they join. You set it here, in the **Create New Class** panel.
Type into the box to search the catalogue, then pick the language the class is learning.
A school on a free trial is held to the one language it signed up for until it subscribes — the picker only shows that course.
steps.terminal: The course is set when the class is made and stays with it. A class that needs a different language is a new class, which keeps the old one's records intact.

walks.title: Choose something else to learn

steps.say: Everything you can get to lives below, and this box is the quick way in. Type a language and the list narrows as you go.
Tap any one of these and you are straight into it — no setting up, no starting over.
Your current course is not going anywhere. Each one keeps its own place, so you can have a poke at a second language and come back without losing an inch in the first.
steps.terminal: That's the Library. Close it and press play to carry on with the one you are in.

walks.title: Play as class or manage it, from the class page

steps.say: **Play as class** starts a whole-class lesson on the class's own account, so the minutes and phrases land on the class, not on you. While a platform admin is viewing this page as you, the button is greyed out and does nothing.
**Manage class** goes to the class's tools: the roster, the teachers, the join link and code, renaming and deleting. The class's practice, minutes and journey stay here on the class page.
steps.terminal: Play from here, manage from there — two different pages, one class. This tour started no lesson and opened no tools.

walks.title: Copy a class link without opening the class

steps.say: On **My Classes**, tap **Copy link** in a class's row — no need to open the class first. Paste it into an email or a lesson slide.
steps.terminal: It's the same link the class page offers, so a student who follows it lands in that class either way.

walks.title: Copy a school's joining links

steps.say: On any school's row, tap **Admin** to copy its admin link or **Teacher** to copy its teacher link — the chip reads Copied so you know it worked. Paste it into an email or message to whoever needs it.
steps.terminal: Tapping a link chip never opens the school — the rest of the row does that. A school still flagged Awaiting admin is one whose admin link nobody has opened yet.

walks.title: Copy a teacher's own play onto the class

steps.say: **Played as themselves by mistake?** — a school leader picks the teacher here. A teacher fixing their own lesson sees no list; the card is about them.
**See what would move** reads the sessions, the time in the app, and where the class will end up. Nothing moves yet.
The teacher keeps their own record either way. Only play on this class's course moves, and the class ends up at the further of the two places.
**Copy onto the class** commits it — one line afterwards says what was copied. Running it again copies nothing twice.
steps.terminal: Preview first, copy only when you're sure. This tour previewed nothing and copied nothing.

walks.title: Copy every teacher's own play onto their class

steps.say: Every teacher in your school who ran lessons signed in as themselves instead of using Play as class, one row per teacher on one class. When there is nothing to copy the card says so in words.
**Copy onto the class** does one row at a time — there is no button that copies everyone at once. The teacher keeps their own record; only play on that class's course moves.
steps.terminal: Row by row, teacher by teacher — that's the whole sweep. This tour copied nothing.

walks.title: Which courses are worth attention

steps.say: **Courses**, under What's happening, is one ranking of every course by real people practising it this month, with how many have ever been in it and how many have reached its end.
The sentence says how many courses are alive this month and which had the most people.
The chart is the courses with anybody in them, most first.

The chips show every course, only the alive ones, or the quiet ones somebody once joined; the chip is written into the page address. Each row carries this month, ever, how many stick and how many finished. Reaching the end means nine tenths of the course, and a course with no recorded length shows a dash. Minutes are left off because the stored counters are not reliable. Open a course row to see which bits of it people stumble on.
steps.terminal: One ranking by people this month. Filter with the chips, open a row for its weak points.

walks.title: Create your first classes

steps.say: Step four of first-time setup. The first row's course is already set to the language you signed up with — change it if this class learns something else.

**+ Add another class** for each further class; every new row starts on that same language. Finishing setup creates every filled-in row, marked Added as it saves. Running the wizard twice will not duplicate classes you've already made.
steps.terminal: One row per class, add as many as you need. This tour created no classes.

walks.title: Download your school's data

steps.say: Under **Data & privacy** in Settings, **Download all data** takes your school's progress figures out of the app as one spreadsheet file — every student, their class, how far they have got, how long they have practised and when they were last active. The file lands in your downloads, named after your school and today's date.
steps.terminal: It is a snapshot of the moment you press the button, not a live link — download it again whenever you want current figures.

walks.title: Email someone their invite again

steps.say: Find the person's row in **Ways in** and tap **Email again**. Nothing changes and no new link is made — the same one they may yet dig out of a spam folder still works.
steps.terminal: Only rows for a named person with an email on file carry this button. If a school's mail gateway is eating our messages, read them the link instead of sending a third time.

walks.title: Look up one student, or take the list away

steps.say: Type part of a name in the search box above the list, or narrow it by class or belt. Each row already carries the learner's belt, their hours this week and when they were last here — often that answers the question on its own. **View** opens what they have actually done on their own account.

**Export CSV** downloads whoever is on screen right now as a spreadsheet file, with today's date in its name. It follows your search and filters, so a narrowed list gives you a narrowed file — clear them first if you want everybody.
steps.terminal: The row records what a learner has done and when they were last here. It makes no judgement about how they are doing.

walks.title: See what a funded organisation gives its learners

steps.say: Tap **Courses** on the organisation's home page.
This is what the organisation hands out through its own sign-up page — given to each learner as they join, not held on the organisation itself.

The courses listed here, and the length of the free period beside them, come from the organisation's enrolment policy. Changing that list is a change to the policy, so it isn't editable here — everyone who has already signed up keeps what they were given.
steps.terminal: That's it — a read-only summary of what this organisation grants on sign-up.

walks.title: See and download your funder numbers

steps.say: **Funder report** is the monthly return your funder asks for, on your own page, so you can read it or send it without asking us to pull it. Three blocks: the month, everything since people enrolled, and the funding year so far. Each block counts everyone and, separately, people aged 16 to 24 — how many registered, how many passed 5, 60 and 100 minutes, and the average minutes.
The month shown is the last complete one. Change it here to report on another month, and the blocks below recompute.
**Download spreadsheet** gives you the same figures as a CSV, ready to send on.
steps.terminal: Minutes here are minutes the app was actually speaking to a learner, never time a screen sat open. Somebody who has studied both Welsh dialects is counted once, at their higher dialect. There are no names in this report and there never will be.

walks.title: Go back over something

steps.say: Nothing is ever locked behind you. Tap here to open the whole course up.
Every belt is listed, with a tick on the ones you have already come through. Open one and you can look through everything you met there.
Choosing something in there does not just show it to you — it moves you to that point and starts you off from there. So use it when you genuinely want to go over old ground, not to peek.
steps.terminal: If you land somewhere you did not mean to, come straight back in here and pick your way forward again. Nothing is lost by wandering.

walks.title: Hand a teacher their access code

steps.say: Tap **Access code** on a teacher's row when email isn't reaching them — school mail gateways quarantine our sign-in codes often enough that this is the rescue, not the exception. It mints a fresh code for them on the spot.
Read the code out, write it down, or paste the link into whatever you already use. They go to saysomethingin.app/join and type it in, then you tap **Done**.
steps.terminal: It works once and lasts two days. Need another? Tap Access code again — the earlier one stops working the moment you do.

walks.title: Hand out a sign-up link for one course

steps.say: On your sign-up link's row in **Ways in**, tap the button named after the course you want — it copies a link that puts a learner straight into that course, no choosing screen. Tap Show all first if the ledger is folded.
steps.terminal: It's the same link and the same cohort either way — the course name only decides where they land, and everyone gets the whole free year whichever link they came through.

walks.title: Hand out your staff links

steps.say: Step two of first-time setup gives you two standing links: copy the **Teacher invite link** for anyone who will run classes, and the **Admin invite link** for anyone who needs to manage the school itself. Send either however you normally reach staff.
steps.terminal: Anyone who has already joined is listed underneath, so you can see who's in as you go. A teacher doesn't need to speak the language — the app does the teaching.

walks.title: Hand a class over to another teacher

steps.say: One teacher on a class is the **lead** — the one the class is listed under, and the one a school admin comes to about it. When you move on from a class, that name should move too.
**Make lead** hands it to a colleague already on the class. It takes effect straight away, so add them first and hand over once you have.
Nothing else moves. The pupils, their progress and every session stay exactly where they are, and you stay on the class as a teacher — you have passed the lead, not left.
steps.terminal: That's handover — the lead is a name, not a wall. Nothing changed while you read this; only your own taps do.

walks.title: How every question page is laid out

steps.say: Every one of the ten questions is answered on a page with the same five parts in the same order. Once you can read one, you can read them all.

The map on the left says who the question is being asked about. **Everyone** asks it of every real person. Tap a course to ask it of that course alone, **Organisations** to pick a group, a school or a class, or **People** to find one person. The choice is written into the page address, so a pasted link asks the same question about the same people.
Across the top of the main column are the things you can do about the answer. When there is nothing to do, the strip is empty rather than missing.
The answer: one plain sentence and one number. Beneath it, when the answer was fetched and who is counted.
The evidence: one chart, never two side by side.
The rows are the things behind the number. Every row is a link to the thing it names.
steps.terminal: Where you are, the answer, the evidence, the rows, the verbs. No page may add a part or move one.

walks.title: Put the app on your device

steps.say: **Your account** holds the two things that are about you rather than your organisation: your sign-in, and the app on the device you are holding.

This row already knows what device you are on. On a computer it offers to install the app in its own window; on a phone it offers to add it to your home screen. Same organisation either way — it just saves you finding the tab.
If your browser can do it in one tap, the button does it. If it cannot, the button walks you through your browser's own menu instead — and you can remove the app again any time, like any other app.
steps.terminal: Nothing here is one-time — if you said no on your first visit, this row is still waiting whenever you change your mind.

walks.title: Invite a teacher who isn't here yet

steps.say: Use this when the colleague has no account yet — a supply teacher starting on Monday, or someone new to the school. It saves waiting for an admin to add them first.
**Create a co-teacher link** mints a fresh link the moment you tap it. Whoever opens it lands as a teacher of this class, and of this school — not as its lead, and not over any of your other classes.
Keep it apart from this one. This is the **student** link — anyone who opens it joins the class as a learner. One link makes a colleague, the other makes a pupil, so send them to the right people.
steps.terminal: Short version: the teacher link is minted per colleague and puts them beside you, the student link is the standing one for the class. This tour minted nothing.

walks.title: Invite a teacher to your school

steps.say: This is one standing link — the same one every time. Tap **Copy invite link** and send it however you reach your staff room: Teams, WhatsApp, printed on a slip. Anyone who opens it signs in once and lands in your list as a teacher.
steps.terminal: Standing in front of them instead? Show code instead gives a short code to read out or write on a whiteboard — they type it in at saysomethingin.com/redeem.

walks.title: Bring your first person in

steps.say: People join through here — tap **Invite a person**. Nothing is created until you submit the form.

Pick **Group leader** for someone who will run a group of their own, or **Learner** for someone who is here to learn. The link carries the role with it, so they arrive already belonging to this group.
With their name filled in, this mints their own sign-in link — the account exists the moment you tap, and the link IS their login. No sign-up, no password. Send it any way you like.
Every link you mint lands here in **Ways in** — you can revoke it or re-mint it any time. Re-minting kills the old link on the spot.
steps.terminal: That's the whole flow — the link is their login. This tour minted nothing; only your own taps do.

walks.title: Bring your first teacher in

steps.say: People join through here — tap **Invite a person**. Nothing is created until you submit the form.
Pick **Teacher** — the link carries the role with it, so whoever clicks it arrives as a teacher of this school.
With their name filled in, this mints their own sign-in link — the account exists the moment you tap, and the link IS their login. Send it any way you like.
Every link you mint lands here in **Ways in** — you can revoke it or re-mint it any time. Re-minting kills the old link on the spot.
steps.terminal: That's the whole flow — the link is their login. This tour minted nothing; only your own taps do.

walks.title: The invites desk

steps.say: Three ways to mint access, one form: **Into an organisation** (role links into the tree), **Direct access** (codes and magic links), **New demo org** (a full practice tree).
**Who** silently changes what the submit button does: some options mint a FRESH link, others surface the STANDING link that already exists. Watch the button label switch as you change this.
Every submit on this desk mints REAL access the moment you tap — a leaked leader link makes a stranger a group leader. This tour never taps it for you.
This pill is not just a badge — tapping it is a live kill-switch. It disables or re-enables the link across all four underlying access mechanisms at once.
steps.terminal: Rule of the desk: look before you mint — everything here is live the moment it exists.

walks.title: Rename, delete or remove a student

steps.say: The pencil beside the class name renames it. Only the name changes — the roster, the join link and the class's place on the course all carry on.

The bin beside the name deletes the class. The app tells you what goes with it first, and asks you to type the class name back if there is real practice behind it. Students keep their own accounts and everything they have learned.
**Remove** at the end of a student's row in the roster takes them off this class only. Their account and everything they've learned stays with them, and they can join another class straight away.
steps.terminal: Rename, delete, remove a student — all from the class's own tools page. This tour changed nothing; only your own taps do.

walks.title: Manage your school's profile, billing and deletion

steps.say: Settings opens on **School profile** — your school's name and details.
**School profile** is where your school's name and details live. Change them here and tap **Save changes** — this is the one place to update it after first-time setup.
Tap **Billing** to see what your school is paying for.

This line is the plain statement of your plan — its name, how many seats it pays for, and whether the subscription is running. **Manage subscription & seats** takes you to the one Upgrade page for any payment change.
Tap **Data & privacy** to reach the danger zone.

**Delete school** closes your school down for good — its classes and everyone's enrolment go with it, and it cannot be undone. A school with real activity in it asks you to type the school's name back before it confirms.
steps.terminal: That's your school's own settings — its name, what it pays, and the one door to close it, all in one place.

walks.title: Minutes in the app this week

steps.say: How much your school practised this week, in minutes, never hours: the time your classes spent in the app with a lesson running, pauses included, plus any teacher or pupil practising on their own account, each counted once. The line beneath is how many of your classes practised at all this week.
steps.terminal: A dash means this week's figures have not loaded yet. Pull to refresh. It is never a zero that is not real.

walks.title: Move a teacher to another class

steps.say: **Teachers** answers 'who teaches this class?'. A head usually wants the other direction too — 'which classes does this person take?' — and that is the same question read backwards.
**Other classes** on anyone's row asks it that way round. It never moves anybody on its own — it opens a list for you to change.
Every class in the school, with the ones this teacher already takes already ticked. Ticking a second, or a third, is all 'belonging to several classes' means — there is no separate step for it.
A move is just both at once: tick where they are going, untick where they are leaving. You are looking at the truth before you change it, so nothing here is a guess.
Saving applies only the boxes you actually changed. If one of them fails, it says which class failed and why, rather than claiming everything saved.
steps.terminal: That's moving a teacher — one untick, one tick, one save. This tour changed nothing; only your own taps do.

walks.title: One person's story

steps.say: **One person** is the page for a support call. Open it from a row on Leaving, or find them under People. The sentence gives their standing, their access and their last practice, and the pill beneath says whether they count as a real person. The verbs across the top act on them: give full access, take it back, make a one-off sign-in link, change their role or trial, or correct a wrong flag. Each verb says what it will change and asks first, and the server records it against your name. The cards below hold their access, memberships, course positions and last few events.
steps.terminal: Everything about one person, on one page, with every change recorded.

walks.title: Open your inbox

steps.say: Tap your name at the top right to open the account menu.
**Inbox** sits near the top, just above Support. The number beside it is how many messages you have not opened yet — the dot on your own avatar is the same count.
steps.terminal: Tap it and you're reading your messages — that count only drops once you open one.

walks.title: Choose which courses a school can use

steps.say: **Courses** sets what a school or group is allowed to learn — the whole catalogue once they're paid up, or a named course or two while they're trialling.
Choose **Trial** and search for the one or two courses it should carry, or **Paid** for the whole catalogue with no per-course picking.

Save, and everyone below that node inherits it. A trial runs for thirty days on a paid course and a year on a free or community one — the server works the dates out on save, so what you see before saving is a preview.
steps.terminal: That's the whole of it — pick Trial or Paid, choose the courses if it's a trial, and save.

walks.title: Play as class from your dashboard

steps.say: **Play as class** on a class card starts a lesson straight from your dashboard, on the class's own account — the minutes and phrases land on the class, not on you.
The player opens on the class's course, at the class's own place in it. While a platform admin is viewing your dashboard as you, this button is greyed out and does nothing.
steps.terminal: One tap from your dashboard, no need to open the class first. This tour started no lesson.

walks.title: Told when you are playing as yourself

steps.say: A line across the top of the player while a lesson runs on your own sign-in rather than on the class — noticed before the minutes land on you. It goes as soon as you pause or stop.

**Your classes** takes you to start the lesson again with Play as class instead. Minutes already played on your own account aren't moved by this line — the copy tool on the class's tools page does that if you want it.
steps.terminal: That's the tell for playing as yourself. This tour moved no minutes.

walks.title: Practice on your own account

steps.say: This line appears under your classes only in a week when your own account has practised. Pressing play on a course from your Library counts for you; only **Play as class** counts for the class. It names your own minutes and when you last played, so a lesson that went to the wrong place is found rather than lost. When it is not here, nothing went astray.
steps.terminal: To move this week's lesson onto the class, open the class and use **Ran a lesson signed in as yourself?** on its tools page.

walks.title: Prove your mailbox reaches you

steps.say: This card appears right after you create a class or copy a class join link, for as long as your own address is unproven. Tap **Send me a code**, or nominate a different address if your school one eats our mail.
Type the six digits we send and tap **That's the one**.
steps.terminal: Close the card instead and it stays closed — it never comes back on a timer.

walks.title: A question whose page is not built yet

steps.say: This is one of the ten questions the surface exists to answer. It has no page yet, and it wears the same layout as the built ones so the bar always shows all ten.
The answer says exactly that: the page has not been built yet. No number is shown because nothing is measured.
Where a chart would be, a card says nothing is measured for this question yet.
steps.terminal: Never a teaser and never a stub with a fake number on it.

walks.title: Read your messages

steps.say: Everything sent to you lands here: a reply on your Support thread, or a notice about something done on your account — like your own practice being copied onto a class. Tap a message to open it, which is what marks it read.
If a message offers **Undo** or **Open Support**, tap that straight from the message. Undo only shows while it can still be done cleanly.
steps.terminal: That's your inbox — nothing here is timed out. A message stays unread until you actually open it, however long it has sat on the list.

walks.title: Reading a class page — practice, journey and students

steps.say: **Class practice** leads, because a class practising together is what a programme lives on. The big figure is how many phrases the class was prompted with together in the last seven days. The line under it says when it last practised and its minutes in the app this week, pauses included. A class that has never played together says so in words and names the teacher's Play as class button as the thing that starts it.

Under the figure are the three phrases the class practised most this week and how many times each came round. A phrase that keeps coming back is the course bringing it back on purpose. Tap **Show all** for the whole list.

**Course journey** is how far the class has travelled, in phrases. A class is one learner account played from the front, so this position is the class's own. The line underneath gives the figure, then names the next belt and how many phrases are left to reach it. Not started is said in words, never drawn as an empty bar.

**Students on their own accounts** is the bonus layer: only pupils who have signed in themselves appear here. Each row carries that student's own position in the course, a small chart of their practice over the past week with the minutes named, and how recently they were active. The dot and word at the start say whether they are excellent, good, needing attention or inactive. Needing attention means nothing for a fortnight or under half the class average, so it is a prompt to look, not a verdict. Tap a row to open that person.
The first three students show. When there are more, tap **Show all** for the rest.
steps.terminal: Class practice first, the class's own journey second, and individual accounts as the layer beneath. This section is only there when at least one pupil has an account of their own.

walks.title: Reading a question page

steps.say: Every night a job reads the week's practice and writes a few findings in plain words. Each lands here, on the question it is about. The dot on a card is its tone: good, watch, alarm or quiet. The line above says when they were found. If that line is red the job has missed two nights or more and the cards are old. It runs from Tom's Mac, not from here.

**Updated** and a time says when the numbers on this page were actually read from the database. It is stamped when the fetch finished, never when the page drew. While it reads **Updating**, nothing on the page is final yet.

This pill says how many real people the numbers are counted from. Demo accounts, SSi staff, class accounts and machine traffic are never people. If a page is deliberately showing demo or staff data the pill says so in red. The count comes from the server, from one shared rule, so two pages can never disagree about who is real.
steps.terminal: Findings above, the answer, then when it was fetched and who it counts. Every question page reads the same way.

walks.title: Reading your insights

steps.say: The **measure** picks what's being counted — progress, practice, class sessions. The line underneath the pickers says exactly what the current one means.
The **window** is the period the rate is computed over — shorter windows react faster, longer ones smooth the noise.
**Compare to** puts an average alongside. Everything here is a rate, not a raw total — so groups of different sizes compare fairly.

This block is the rate itself, beside whatever you are comparing to. It is an amount per learner per week, never a running total — a total only says how big and how old a place is, a rate says how fast it is moving, which is what you can act on.

**Practising** answers whether your classes are doing it: how many practised together this week against last week, the phrases practised each day over four weeks, and which people practised on their own account and for how long.
**Quiet** is the half you act on: which classes practised before and have stopped, how long ago, and which have never started. Open a class row to see where it stopped.
**Journey** shows where in the course each class has got to, as the last phrase it played in both languages, and the funnel shows the sentence most classes stop before. Class rows run furthest first.

**Voice and pause** is what the microphone is giving us below this level. Read the uptake figure first — it is how many learners the rest is based on. A learner with no mic data is absent here, never a zero.
**Overview** and **Insights** are two tabs on the same place. Overview takes you back to its home — insights is a lens on where you already are, not a different page to get lost in.
steps.terminal: Rates lead, position is context — and the picker text always says what a measure means.

walks.title: How many in-app minutes are being done

steps.say: The first question: how many in-app minutes are being done, per course, in total and per person, and how each course stands against the average of all courses. A minute is everything between pressing play and stopping, on every screen.
Pick the **window**: today, the last seven days or the last thirty days. The course picker beside it opens on the busiest course in that window.
Pick the **measure**: minutes per person, minutes in total, new enrolments, or people with no activity. The line under the pickers says what it counts and what the average of all courses is for it.

Two numbers: this course against the average of all courses, and the strip beneath for where the course sits among the rest. The average counts this course too, and a course with two enrolments weighs two people, not a whole course.
The rows count the real people who practised in the last fourteen days, by course. Open one to see which bits of that course give trouble.
steps.terminal: Every minute here is the same minute every school page shows, and a person on the course who did not press play still counts in the denominator.

walks.title: Reading the course list

steps.say: Each card names the language you would be learning, and under it, the language it would be taught in. That second line is the one worth reading — it is what you will hear the prompts in.
The right-hand side tells you where you stand. A coloured dot and a position means you have already started that one and it is holding your place for you.

**Premium** with **Try free** next to it means the course is a paid one, and that you can properly get going in it first. You carry on until the app asks — nothing stops you mid-thought and nothing is taken before you have said yes.
Some languages offer more than one card — a different region or accent of the same language. Pick whichever you would rather end up sounding like.
steps.terminal: Nothing here commits you. Tapping a card takes you into it, and every course you have touched keeps its own place waiting.

walks.title: Reading your class list

steps.say: One row per class. Belt, how far through the course, minutes played as class this week and the shape of those days — all the class account's own, never a pupil's.
**Course** narrows the list to one language. **Sort by** puts it in the order that answers your question — name, journey, or phrases practised.
Tiles by year, read off the class name — **7B** and **Year 9 French** both count. Tap a tile and the table narrows to that year.
Anywhere on a row opens that class. The buttons at the right end do their own jobs and do not open it.
steps.terminal: That's reading the list — the row itself opens a class. This tour opened nothing.

walks.title: Remove a teacher from your school

steps.say: **Remove** on a teacher's row takes them off your school when they leave, or clears out a name you don't recognise under Not yet given classes. You'll be asked to confirm their name back before it happens.
steps.terminal: Their own account survives — what goes is their place in this school and their view of its classes. An admin's row carries no Remove button at all, so you can never lose your own admin this way.

walks.title: Report a bug from Settings

steps.say: Under **Tools** in Settings sits **Report a bug** — tap it to open the sheet. Nothing is sent until you tap Send on it.
This sheet is the whole flow — one box, one optional screenshot, one Send. Tap outside it and it closes without sending anything.
Write what you saw in your own words here. Your course and device details are added for you, so you only need to describe the problem itself.

**Send** stays off until you have written something. You would tap **Send** here — press Next to continue without sending. When you do send for real it reads **Sending…** while your note, and your screenshot if you added one, goes.
steps.terminal: Once it lands, **Got it, thank you** replaces the form — that line is the whole reply. The sheet closes on its own a moment later, or tap the line to close it now. Nobody replies through the app: your note goes to one place where we read it, whether or not you are signed in.

walks.title: Report a bug from the dashboard

steps.say: Tap your name at the top right to open the account menu.
**Report a bug** sits in that menu — tap it to open the window without leaving the dashboard. The page you are on, and your school, are attached for you.
Write what you saw, or what you would like to see, in **What happened?**. Add what you expected underneath if that helps — that part is optional.

**Send** stays off until you have written something. You would tap **Send** here — press Next to continue without sending. When you do send for real it reads **Sending…** while your note goes, with your screenshot too if you added one.
steps.terminal: A **Got it, thank you** toast appears at the top of the page and that is the whole reply — nobody answers through the app. Questions about the dashboard itself go to Support instead.

walks.title: Run your first class session

steps.say: Students join with this link — share it and they sign up straight into this class.
Prefer a whiteboard? **Show code instead** reveals a standing code — anyone who enters it at saysomethingin.com/redeem joins this class, until the code changes.
**Play as class** is the heart of it: one device — yours — leads the whole class through a session, and it counts for every student on the roster.
steps.terminal: When you're ready, tap Play as class for real — this tour never starts a session for you.

walks.title: Save your progress

steps.say: Right now everything you have done lives on this device alone. It works perfectly well — but a cleared browser or a new phone takes it with it.
Tap this and you give us an email address, nothing more. We send you a code, you type it in, and your position is yours on any device you sign in on.
steps.terminal: Everything you have already done comes with you — signing in adds your account to it, it never starts you again.

walks.title: Which addresses look like your school

steps.say: Type the part of your school's email after the @, such as example.sch.uk, and tap **Add domain**. Nobody is let in or kept out by this — it only sorts your Not yet given classes list, so an arrival from a domain you don't recognise rises to the top.
For one named person on a personal address — a supply teacher, a colleague without a school email — type their address here and tap **Add address** instead.
**Remove** beside any entry takes it off the list. Nothing is revoked — the person just stops being sorted to the top as unfamiliar.
steps.terminal: That's the whole list — it changes ordering, never access. Giving somebody a class is what actually brings them into your school.

walks.title: Set your language and time zone

steps.say: Tap **Localisation** to choose the language the dashboard speaks to you in, and the time zone your dates and times are read against.

Pick your interface language and time zone, then tap **Save changes**. This is remembered on the device you set it on — teachers and students each choose their own, so it doesn't change what anybody else sees.
steps.terminal: That's the whole thing — one language, one time zone, always changeable, always in the same place.

walks.title: See every school in your programme

steps.say: Every school you look after, one row each, with its students, teachers, classes and practice hours side by side. The totals above the table are the programme as a whole. Search by name to find one school, or sort by name, hours or students. A school with nobody running it yet is flagged in the Status column as awaiting admin. Tap any row to open that school's own dashboard.
steps.terminal: The list holds still until you refresh it, so a number will not change under you while you read. If a refresh fails you are told plainly rather than shown stale figures as current.

walks.title: Seeing how it is going — the numbers and the map on any level

steps.say: This map stays down the side of every level. Read it top to bottom: the levels above you, the one you are on, its neighbours and what sits under it. Tap any name to move straight there — the page rebuilds around it and the map redraws.

**Updated** and a time says when these figures were last fetched. Reload the page to fetch again and the stamp moves with it. An empty stamp means the numbers have not arrived yet, not that they are old.

The row of numbers counts everything below this level, each person once. **Phrases practised this week** and **Classes practising this week** come from whole-class play over the last seven days. **Minutes in the app this week** is time in the lesson, pauses included, for the classes below and for staff and students on their own accounts. On your own school each card is a link to the list behind it.

**By year group** splits the same minutes by year: **Y7**, **Y8** and so on, read off each class name, with the minutes this week beneath and how many of that year's classes practised out of how many there are. **Other** holds classes whose names carry no year. If fewer than half your class names carry a year, the card reads **By class** instead.

**Below this** draws everything hanging beneath here — groups inside groups, their classes, the teachers who take them and staff who teach nothing yet. Tap a caret to open or close a branch, tap a name to go to that level. A class row already tells you its teachers, its student count and whether it practised together this week, so you need not open it to find out.
steps.terminal: The map tells you where you are, the numbers tell you how it is going below here, and the tree takes you down a level whenever you want the detail.

walks.title: Set or change your password

steps.say: **Your account** is your own corner of this page — not the organisation's, yours. Your sign-in and your device live here, and nothing in it is visible to anyone you have invited.
If you arrived through a **link in an email**, that link will not last forever. A password is how you get back into your organisation from a new laptop, a new phone, or after clearing your browser.
Tap **Set a password** and the form opens right here. You will sign in with your email address and that password from then on — and you can come back and change it any time.
steps.terminal: That is the whole thing — one password, always changeable, always in the same place.

walks.title: Choose which courses your school uses

steps.say: Step three of first-time setup, **Choose courses** — everything your school has access to starts ticked here.
Untick anything you don't plan to teach. This is a filter and nothing more — it doesn't change what your school has access to, it just shortens the list you pick from at the next step.
steps.terminal: Tap Continue and step four's course picker only offers what you left ticked here.

walks.title: Give a class its course

steps.say: Step four, **Create classes** — each class row already holds the language you signed your school up with, so most classes need nothing done here.
To teach something else, tap the picker and start typing — the catalogue runs to dozens of courses, and this only offers what you left ticked at Choose courses.
Pick the one you want. Where a language offers more than one version, the versions differ by region or accent.
steps.terminal: Save the class and everyone who joins it lands in that course.

walks.title: Share a class with a colleague

steps.say: A class does not have to be yours alone. **Teachers** lists everyone who teaches it, with the lead marked — a job share, a department colleague, a supply teacher covering for a fortnight.
**Add another teacher** is how you share it. Nobody is added until you pick a name and confirm.
You can pick anyone already teaching at your school. If the list is empty, your colleague has not joined the school yet — the link underneath brings them straight in.
What they get is the whole class: the roster, the sessions, the progress, and the right to run a class session. What they do not get is the lead — that stays with you until you hand it over.
steps.terminal: That's sharing a class — same class, two teachers, one lead. This tour added nobody; only your own taps do.

walks.title: Start a session or make a class from the list

steps.say: **Play as class** at the end of a row starts a session straight from the list — no need to open the class first. Your device leads, the whole class moves on together.
**+ New class** sets up a class of your own: a name, a language, and a join link made for you at the same moment.
**Export CSV** takes the list away as a spreadsheet — belt, journey, minutes, join code, one row per class. What you export is whatever the filters currently show.
steps.terminal: Starting a session, making a class, exporting the list — all from the same page. This tour started nothing and made nothing.

walks.title: Add, rename and delete schools and groups

steps.say: **Add a school** creates a school inside this group, with its own home page, its own staff and its own learners. This verb only shows on a plain group — a school can't contain another school.
**Mint a demo org** stands up a whole organisation with plausible people and activity already in it, for showing somebody what the product looks like once it's running.
**Rename** changes what this school or group is called everywhere it appears. Nothing else moves — the same people, classes and links carry on under the new name.

**Delete** is the one verb here that takes everything below it with it. You're shown what goes — classes, people and links — and asked to type the name back before it confirms whenever there's real activity underneath.
steps.terminal: Everything here works the same way — open the school or group, and its verbs sit in a row along the top.

walks.title: Subscribe as a tutor

steps.say: Choose Monthly or Annual — annual works out at two months free — then tap **Subscribe** and fill in the card details on the panel that opens. It's one seat, for you; your students pay for their own learning separately, and three paying students cover what your dashboard costs.
steps.terminal: Once it's running, this same button becomes **Manage subscription** for invoices and cancellation.

walks.title: Subscribe your organisation and change its seats

steps.say: This line always tells the truth about who's actually joined against how many seats you're paying for — before you subscribe it previews what you're about to pay for, and it never blocks a class from running even if more people join than you've paid seats for.

Choose Monthly or Annual, set the number of learner seats with the stepper — it opens at the number of people already joined — then tap **Subscribe** and fill in the card details on the panel that opens.

Once you're subscribed, this same spot becomes **Update to N seats** — step the count up or down any time your organisation grows or shrinks, and it changes against your existing subscription with no second charge.
steps.terminal: One subscription covers every seat and every language across the group, and you can add or remove seats whenever you need to.

walks.title: Subscribe your school and change its seats

steps.say: This line always tells the truth about how many teachers have joined against how many seats you're paying for — nothing is ever blocked, it just shows you the gap so you can put it right.

Choose Monthly or Annual, set the number of teacher seats with the stepper — it opens at the number of teachers who've actually joined — then tap **Subscribe** and fill in the card details on the panel that opens. Seats are teacher seats; your students don't each need one.
Once you're subscribed, this same spot becomes **Update to N seats** — step it up or down any time staff join or leave, changed against your existing subscription with no second charge.
steps.terminal: That's a trial turned into a paid school, with the same page covering it for as long as your staff numbers change.

walks.title: Take a teacher off a class, or move them

steps.say: **Assign to a class** on a teacher's row opens their ticks — the classes they take now, already ticked.
The ticks start from what is true today, so moving somebody from one class to another is a single change rather than two.
Untick the class they're leaving, tick the one they're joining. A move is one change here, not two.
**Save** counts your changes back to you before it commits. If part of it fails, the panel stays open and names the class it couldn't do — nothing is ever reported saved when it wasn't.
steps.terminal: Untick, tick, save — that's moving or removing a teacher. This tour changed nobody's classes.

walks.title: Ways in — who can get in, and how to change it

steps.say: Every way in, in one ledger: personal sign-in links and shareable join links, for everywhere below here. With more than three links it folds to one row per role — how many, and how often they have been used.
Tap **Show all** to open the full ledger, every link on its own row with its own verbs. You can filter by role or by place with the chips once it is open.
**Copy** re-shares the same live link — always safe, nothing changes.

**Re-mint** sits on a person's OWN sign-in link, and only there: it makes that person a new link and the old one stops working the moment you tap — if they bookmarked the old one they are locked out until you send them the new one. A shareable link has no Re-mint, because there is nobody to re-bind it to.
**Revoke** switches a link off. It's undoable — a revoked row grows a **Put back** button. For a shareable link this is how you retire it: revoke the old one, then make a fresh one.

And this is where a brand-new shareable link comes from — **Get a shareable link** at the top of this page, one per role. **Invite a person** next to it makes a personal link for someone you can name.
steps.terminal: The short version: copy is safe, revoke can always be undone, re-mint is for one person's own link — and a new shareable link is made at the top of the page, not in the ledger.

walks.title: Which bits of a course make people stumble

steps.say: **Weak points**, under What's happening, shows for one course which pieces of it real learners skip, retry or stop on, ranked by how much trouble each piece caused per person who met it. Pick a course under **Courses** in the map on the left first; until you do, the page waits.

The sentence names the piece that gave people the most trouble. When fewer than five real people have practised the course, the page says **too few to say** instead of a number. That is the truth about the course, not a fault in the page.
The rows are the bits, worst first, each showing both languages with its skips, retries, failures and the share of people who stopped there. Open a row to see that piece and its phrases.
steps.terminal: Pick a course, read the worst piece, open a row to see its phrases.

walks.title: Where a class's practice is read

steps.say: A class has two pages. This one is its tools: the roster, the teachers, the join link, renaming and deleting. What the class has practised together, its minutes in the app and how far it has travelled live on the class page — the link in this line takes you there. Nothing on this page totals whole-class play.

**Students on their own accounts** lists the pupils who have signed in as themselves and joined this class, one row each, with their belt, what they have learned, how much they have practised on that account and when they were last at it. Type a name into the search box to jump to one of them.
steps.terminal: This table counts only what each pupil did signed in as themselves. A class taught from the front with no pupil accounts has nobody here, and that is not a class that has done nothing.

walks.title: What your classes actually practised

steps.say: **What they practised this week** is the teaching story rather than the register: the phrases the classes beneath this level practised together in the last seven days. Three columns — the prompt, the phrase the class practised, and how many times it came round. The three most practised come first, and you can tap a column heading to sort. A phrase that appears again and again is the course bringing it back on purpose, which is how it sticks. Only whole-class play counts here; what staff and students do on their own accounts is in the minutes figure above.
Tap **Show all** to see every phrase. **Show fewer** folds the list back to the top three.
steps.terminal: A level whose classes have not played together this week says so in words instead of showing an empty list.

walks.title: What your numbers mean

steps.say: These are a record of what you have already done. None of them is a target, and none of them is being compared with anybody.
Time is the time you have actually spent learning. If it ever shows a **~** in front of it, that is us working it out from how far along you are, because we have not logged the sessions themselves.
Phrases learnt is how many separate phrases every one of your courses has introduced you to so far. It is added up across all of them, so it grows whichever language you pick up.
steps.terminal: Nothing here changes what you get next. The course follows your position, not these numbers.

walks.title: Where in the world people are using us, and on what

steps.say: **Where and what**, under What's happening, answers two questions at once: which countries real people practised from in the last thirty days, and whether they were on phones, tablets or desktops, in the app or in a browser. Machine traffic is left out by rule.
The sentence gives you how many real people, from how many countries, and the country and device most of them are on. A person seen on two devices is counted once here and once under each device.
The chart is people by country, most first.

One row per country, each with its phone, tablet and desktop split and its in-the-app or in-a-browser split. Tap a country to narrow the page to it; tap a device chip to count only that device. Both choices are written into the page address, so a pasted link reproduces the view. In the app or in a browser has only been recorded since 10 September 2026, so earlier people read as not recorded rather than being guessed at.
steps.terminal: Countries and devices on one page. Tap a country or a device chip to narrow it, and the address carries the choice.

walks.title: Where the class has got to

steps.say: **Course Journey** is how far your class has travelled through its course, as a bar in phrases. A class is one learner account played from the front, so this is the class's own place on the course, moved by the sessions you run together. The line under the bar says how many phrases are left to the next belt.
steps.terminal: A class that has never played says Not started in words. It is never shown as a bar of zero.

walks.title: Where you are in this course

steps.say: This card is your whole position in the course in one glance. Nothing here is a score, and nothing here is counting anything against you.

Those eight coloured dots are **belts**, and the filled one is where you are now. A belt marks how far along the course you have come — it is a position, not a grade, and there is nothing to pass. You move to the next one simply by carrying on.
The bar underneath lays the whole course out end to end, with each belt as its own band of colour. The marker on it is you — so it shows how far you have come rather than how far is left.
Tap the card itself to open the belts up. You can look through everything you have met so far, and start again from any point you fancy revisiting.
steps.terminal: That's your position. Close this whenever you like and press play — it always picks up exactly where you left off.

walks.title: Who is about to leave

steps.say: **Leaving**, under What's happening, is the list of who to write to and why: real people who were practising regularly and have stopped, paying people who have gone quiet, and people whose access runs out within a fortnight. This page sends nothing.
The sentence says how many, and why.
The chart is how long they have been gone.

The rows are ordered by who was seen most recently, then by who was most regular before they stopped. Nobody is ranked by money, because no amount is stored for anyone. Each row carries every reason that applies, how long since they were seen, how regular they were, and when their access ends if it is ending. Open a row to see that person and act on them.
steps.terminal: Who has gone quiet and why, most recently seen first. Open a row to write to them.

walks.title: Name your school and work through setup

steps.say: First-time setup is four short steps, listed down the left — your school, your staff, your courses, your classes. Tap any of them to jump straight to it, forwards or back.
Type your school's name as you would write it on a letterhead — this is what your teachers and students see on every page and every invite link.

**Save & exit** saves the step you're on and puts you back on your dashboard, so you never have to finish setup in one sitting. Come back to Settings and First-time setup whenever you want to carry on.
steps.terminal: Everything the wizard sets up can also be changed later from Settings and from your class pages — nothing here is a one-shot.

walks.title: Whether the app is working right now

steps.say: **Working now**, under What's happening, tells you whether audio is failing for real people, on which build and on which kind of device, so you can see whether the last fix reached them. Only real people's plays count, so your own session on staging is not here.
The sentence gives the failure rate over the last seven days and the build most people are on today.
The chart is the failure rate by day.

One row per build, most people first, with people, plays, how many failed and the rate. The build most people are on today carries a pill. Tap a build to narrow the rows to it; the choice is written into the page address. The line under the rows is the same rate for phones against desktops.
steps.terminal: Rate by day, then by build, then by device. If a fix landed, the newest build's row is where you see it.

walks.title: Find out which email you are signed in with

steps.say: At the top of **Account** in Settings is the address this account uses. Tap it and it copies — useful the moment you sign in on a new device and cannot remember which email you used.
Under it is your account code. Tap that to copy it too, and give it to us if you ever get in touch — it names your account and nothing more, so it is safe to read out or put in a message.
steps.terminal: That's the whole card — your address and your code, both a tap away from your clipboard.

walks.title: Your class against the average

steps.say: **Your classes** picks which of your classes you are reading. If you teach only one, this picker stays out of the way and the page is already about that class.
The **measure** is what is being counted — the line underneath says exactly what the current one means.
The **window** is the period the rate is worked out over. Shorter windows react faster, longer ones smooth the noise.
**Compare to** sets your class's rate beside an average. Everything here is a rate, not a raw total, so a class of eight and a class of thirty compare fairly.
steps.terminal: This answers whether a class is moving well, which a roster of totals cannot. A class with too few sessions to compare honestly says so rather than showing a number built from nothing.

walks.title: Your classes at a glance

steps.say: Every class you teach is here, one entry each, with its course beside it. Tap the class name to open its class page.

This is the class's own week: the minutes it spent in the app with a lesson running, the phrases it practised, and how far it has travelled through the course. Those minutes come from the lessons you ran with **Play as class**. A class that has never played says **Not started** in words.
Kept apart, and never added in, is what the pupils did on their own accounts this week. When there is nothing it says so in words, which is usual for a class taught from the front.

Under your classes, one quiet line totals them: how many classes you teach, the minutes they spent in the app this week with a lesson running, pauses included, and the phrases they were prompted with. All of it is the classes' own play from the front.
The second line is the minutes your pupils spent on their own accounts this week, kept apart from the first and never added to it.
steps.terminal: The join code on each class is what you read out to get a new pupil in.

handbook.title: A question whose page is not built yet
handbook.what: Holding the place of a question that is in the frame but has no page yet, in the same layout as the built ones, so the bar always shows all ten and nothing pretends to measure what it does not.
handbook.where: Any of the ten questions in the bar that has no page yet.
how: Tap the question in the bar.
Read the card saying nothing is measured for it yet.
handbook.note: This is never a teaser and never a stub with a fake number on it.

handbook.title: Add a class to a group
handbook.what: Creating a class underneath a group you lead, before anyone is teaching it. Useful when you are setting a term up in advance and will put a teacher on each class later.
handbook.where: The group's own page, the **Add a class** button in the row of actions at the top.
how: Open the group the class belongs under.
Tap **Add a class**.
Type the class name.
Choose the course the class will learn.
Tap **Add**.
handbook.note: A class needs no teacher to exist. It sits under the group waiting, and you put a teacher on it whenever you are ready. The course must be one your group has cover for. A paid language you have not subscribed to and are not trialling is refused when you tap **Add**, and the message says so.

handbook.title: Add a school to your programme
handbook.what: Creating a new school inside your programme. The school exists the moment you name it, already attached to your group, with its admin link and teacher link ready to hand over.
handbook.where: All schools, the **+ Add school** button at the top right.
how: Tap **+ Add school**.
Type the school's name and tap **Create school**.
Copy the Admin link and send it to whoever will run the school — opening it takes them straight to sign-in as its admin.
Copy the Teacher link too if you are setting their staff up as well.
Tap **Done**. The new school appears in the list.
handbook.note: There is no separate onboarding step to remember. Both links live on the school's row from then on, so you can fetch them again any time.

handbook.title: Add a school under a group
handbook.what: Creating a school inside a group, so it has its own home page, its own staff and its own learners while still rolling up into whatever sits above it.
handbook.where: The group's home page, **Add a school** along the top.
how: Open the home page of the group the school belongs under.
Tap **Add a school**.
Type the school's name.
Tap **Add**, and the school appears in the list below.
handbook.note: The verb only shows on a plain group. A school cannot contain another school, and an organisation using the neutral wording has groups rather than schools all the way down.

handbook.title: Add a student to a class
handbook.what: Making one learner their own way into one class. The link puts them straight into that class with no forms and no sign-up, so a child can be learning within a minute of opening it.
handbook.where: The class's own page, **Invite students** along the top.
how: Open the class.
Tap **Invite students**.
Type the student's name.
Add their email if you want us to send it, or leave it blank and you get a link to hand over yourself.
Submit, and repeat for the next student.
handbook.note: One student at a time, on purpose — the link is theirs alone and carries the class with it. The **Students** page's **+ Invite students** button brings you here for exactly this reason.

handbook.title: Add a teacher by name
handbook.what: Adding a specific teacher to your school when you know who they are but cannot rely on email reaching them. You type their name and get a code to hand over yourself.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, the **Add by name** button at the top.
how: Tap **Add by name**.
Type the teacher's name.
Tap **Create code**.
Read the code out, write it down, or paste it into whatever you already use to reach them.
They go to saysomethingin.app/join and type it in.
handbook.note: They appear on your list straight away under **Not yet given classes**, so you can tick their classes before they have even signed in. The code works once and lasts two days, and whoever uses it becomes that person — so hand it over directly. Made a mistake? Remove them from the list.

handbook.title: Add students to a class
handbook.what: Putting a pupil who is already in your school into this class, for a pupil who has changed set or landed in the wrong class.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Add students** button at the top of the roster.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Tap **Add students** above the roster.
Type a few letters of the name to narrow the list.
Tap the pupil. They appear on the roster straight away.
Add as many as you need, then tap **Done**.
handbook.note: The list holds the pupils in your school who are not in this class yet, and under each name are the classes they are in now, or **In no class**. Adding does not take them out of those classes — a pupil can be in more than one, one for each course they are doing. If you meant to move them, the message that confirms the add names the class they are still in and takes you to it, where their row has a **Remove** button. A pupil brings everything they have already learned with them. For a pupil with no account at all, use the class link in **Invite students** instead.

handbook.title: Bring your first person in
handbook.what: Bringing anyone into this part of the tree — a leader, a teacher or a learner — with a personal link that is their login.
handbook.where: The node's home page, the buttons along the top, **Invite a person**.
how: Open the group, school or organisation you want them to belong to.
Tap **Invite a person**.
Pick the role they arrive as.
Type their name and submit.
Copy the minted link and send it.
handbook.note: Nothing is created until you submit. Every link you mint lands in **Ways in**.

handbook.title: Change how many seats you pay for
handbook.what: Growing or shrinking a live subscription as staff or learners come and go, without going through checkout a second time.
handbook.where: The Upgrade page, once you are already subscribed. The stepper sits beside the running total.
how: Open the Upgrade page.
Step the seat count up or down, or type the number straight in.
The button changes to read Update, with the new monthly total on it.
Tap it. The change is made against your existing subscription — no second charge and no new card details.
handbook.note: While the count matches what you already pay for, the button simply says current and does nothing, so you cannot double-bill yourself by tapping it twice.

handbook.title: Change your school's name and details
handbook.what: Correcting or updating what the app knows about your school — its name, its town, its contact email and a short description. The name is the one that shows on every page your staff and students see.
handbook.where: Settings, then School profile.
how: Open Settings and stay on School profile.
Edit any of the fields — school name, city, region, contact email, about.
Tap **Save changes**. The button reads Saved when it has gone through.
The new name appears across the dashboard straight away.
handbook.note: Only a school admin can edit this. A teacher opening the same page sees the details but cannot change them. Your school's type is set by your group administrator, not here.

handbook.title: Choose what a class learns
handbook.what: Setting the language a class learns. Every class carries one course, and it decides what the class practises, what students hear when they join, and where the class's shared position sits.
handbook.where: The **Create New Class** panel, the **Course / Language** picker.
how: Tap **+ New class** on **My Classes**.
Type into the course box to search the catalogue.
Pick the language the class is learning.
Finish creating the class.
handbook.note: The course is set when the class is made and stays with it. A class that needs a different language is a new class, which keeps the old one's records intact. A school on a free trial is held to the one language it signed up for until it subscribes.

handbook.title: Choose what role someone arrives as
handbook.what: The role you pick on an invite is the role the person lands in, and it travels with the link rather than being set afterwards. Teacher sees their own classes, group leader sees everything below their node, learner just learns.
handbook.where: Any node's home page, **Invite a person**, the role dropdown on the left of the form.
how: Tap **Invite a person** on the node you want them to belong to.
Open the role dropdown.
Pick the role they should hold in this place.
Fill in their name and submit.
handbook.note: The place matters as much as the role — a group leader invited on a group leads that group and everything under it, so invite people on the node whose shape you actually mean.

handbook.title: Choose which courses a school can use
handbook.what: Setting what a school or group is allowed to learn: the whole catalogue when they are paid up, or a named course or two while they are trialling.
handbook.where: The node's home page, **Courses** along the top.
how: Open the home page of the school or group.
Tap **Courses**.
Choose the whole catalogue, or search for the courses the trial should carry.
Save, and everyone below that node inherits it.
handbook.note: A trial runs for thirty days on a paid course and a year on a free or community one, and the server works the dates out on save — what you see before saving is a preview.

handbook.title: Choose which courses your school uses
handbook.what: Narrowing the full list of courses your school can teach down to the handful you actually intend to use, so that choosing a course for a class is a short list rather than a long one.
handbook.where: Step three of first-time setup, the grid of tickable course tiles under **Choose courses**.
how: Open step three of first-time setup.
Everything available to your school starts ticked.
Untick anything you do not plan to teach.
Tap **Continue** — the next step only offers the courses you left ticked.
handbook.note: This is a filter and nothing more. It does not change what your school has access to, and it takes nothing away from anyone. A school on a trial sees its one trial course here; a subscribed school sees the whole catalogue.

handbook.title: Choosing who a question is asked about
handbook.what: Asking the same question of a smaller group: everyone, one course, one organisation or one person. The question does not change; who it is about does.
handbook.where: The map on the left of every question page, the same map the organisation dashboard draws. On a phone it is the first block.
how: Tap **Everyone** to ask the question of every real person.
Tap a course to ask it of that course alone. The other courses stay one tap away as the rows at this level.
Tap **Organisations** to go to the organisation tree and pick a group, a school or a class.
Tap **People** to find one person by name or email.
handbook.note: The choice is written into the page address, so a pasted link opens the same question about the same people.

handbook.title: Claim another email domain for your school
handbook.what: Telling the app which email domains belong to your school, so an arrival using one of them is not pushed to the top of your **Not yet given classes** list as somebody unfamiliar. Your own domain was recorded when you signed up; add the others if your school uses more than one.
handbook.where: Settings, the **Which addresses look like your school** card, the **Add domain** field.
how: Open Settings and find **Which addresses look like your school**.
Type the part of the address after the @, such as example.sch.uk.
Tap **Add domain**.
handbook.note: This grants nothing. Somebody at your domain still sees no learner until you give them a class, and somebody who is not still gets in with one tap. Public providers such as gmail.com or outlook.com cannot be added, because they do not identify a school. Schools in the same trust share each other's domains automatically.

handbook.title: Copy a class link without opening the class
handbook.what: Grabbing a class's join link straight from the class list, for when you are sending links to several classes in one sitting.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the **Copy link** button in each row.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Find the class's row.
Tap **Copy link**.
Paste it into your email or your lesson slide.
handbook.note: It is the same link the class page offers, so a student who follows it lands in that class either way.

handbook.title: Copy a school's joining links
handbook.what: Fetching the admin link or the teacher link for any school in your programme, so you can chase a school that has not got started or replace a link somebody has lost.
handbook.where: All schools, the Links column on each school's row.
how: Find the school's row in the list.
Tap **Admin** to copy its admin link, or **Teacher** to copy its teacher link.
The chip reads Copied so you know it worked.
Paste it into an email or a message to whoever needs it.
handbook.note: Tapping a link chip does not open the school — the rest of the row does that. A school still flagged as awaiting admin is one whose admin link nobody has opened yet.

handbook.title: Copy a teacher's own play onto the class
handbook.what: Putting right a class whose teacher ran a lesson signed in as themselves instead of using Play as class, so the class carries the progress it really made. A teacher fixes their own lesson; a school leader can fix any teacher's.
handbook.where: The class page and the class tools page, the **Ran a lesson signed in as yourself?** card. A school leader's card is headed **Played as themselves by mistake?** and has a list to pick the teacher from.
how: As a school leader, pick the teacher from the list. As a teacher there is no list: the card is about you.
Tap **See what would move** and read the sessions, the time in the app and where the class will be afterwards.
Tap **Copy onto the class**. One line tells you what was copied.
handbook.note: The teacher keeps their own record. Only play on this class's course moves, the class ends up at the further of the two places, and running it again copies nothing twice. While viewing as someone else you can see what would move but not copy it.

handbook.title: Copy every teacher's own play onto their class
handbook.what: Finding every teacher in your school who ran lessons signed in as themselves instead of using Play as class, and moving that play onto their class, one teacher at a time. Each row names the class, the teacher, what would move, and where the class will be afterwards.
handbook.where: Your school's own page, the one you land on, under the row of numbers and above what your classes practised.
how: Read down the rows. Each is one teacher on one class.
Tap **Copy onto the class** on a row. One line tells you what was copied and where the class now is.
Do the next row when you are ready. There is no button that copies everyone at once.
handbook.note: The teacher keeps their own record. Only play on that class's course moves, the class ends up at the further of the two places, and copying the same teacher again moves nothing twice. A teacher who is on two classes for the same course appears on two rows with the same play: the row says so, and a lesson goes onto one class only, so once you have copied it the other row has nothing left to copy. When there is nothing to copy the card says so in words. While viewing as someone else you can read the rows but not copy.

handbook.title: Create your first classes
handbook.what: Setting up the classes your school will actually teach. A class is a name, a course and the students who join it, and it is the thing every progress figure in the dashboard is eventually counted against.
handbook.where: Step four of first-time setup, under **Create classes**. **+ Add another class** sits below the rows.
how: Open step four of first-time setup.
Type a class name in the first row. Its course is already set to the language you signed your school up with — change it if this class is learning something else.
Tap **+ Add another class** for each further class; every new row starts on that same language, and fills in the same way.
Remove a row you no longer want with the cross at its end.
Tap **Finish setup** — every filled-in row is created, and each one is marked Added as it saves.
handbook.note: Classes you have already made are listed above the rows, so running the wizard twice will not duplicate them. Students are added from each class's own page whenever you are ready.

handbook.title: Delete a class
handbook.what: Removing a class you no longer want, usually one set up by mistake or a group that has finished. Before anything is deleted the app tells you what goes with it.
handbook.where: The class page, the small bin beside the class name.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Tap the bin next to the name at the top.
Read the list of what will go with the class.
If the class has real practice behind it, type the class name to confirm you mean it.
Confirm the deletion.
handbook.note: Students keep their own accounts and everything they have learned. What goes is the class itself, its roster and its join link.

handbook.title: Delete a school or group
handbook.what: Removing a school or group that should never have existed, or has been wound up. It is the one verb here that takes everything below it with it.
handbook.where: The node's home page, **Delete** at the end of the row of buttons.
how: Open the home page of the school or group.
Tap **Delete**.
Read the summary of what goes with it — classes, people and links are counted for you.
Type the name back when asked, and confirm.
handbook.note: You are only asked to type the name when there is real activity underneath, which is the signal to stop and check. An empty shell deletes on a single confirm.

handbook.title: Delete your school
handbook.what: Closing your school down for good. It removes the school itself along with its classes and everybody's enrolment in them, and it cannot be undone.
handbook.where: Settings, then Data & privacy, at the bottom under Danger zone.
how: Open Settings and choose Data & privacy.
Scroll to Danger zone and tap **Delete school**.
Read what the app lists as going with it — classes, students, teachers and recorded sessions are each counted for you.
If the school has real activity in it, type the school's name exactly to confirm you mean it.
Confirm. You are signed out to a clean slate, because the account you were using belonged to a school that no longer exists.
handbook.note: Only your own school can be deleted this way, and only by its admin. A school with nothing in it deletes without the typed confirmation; one with students and sessions always asks for it.

handbook.title: Download your school's data
handbook.what: Taking your school's progress figures out of the app as a spreadsheet file — every student, the class they are in, how far they have got, how long they have practised and when they were last active.
