handbook.where: Settings, then Data & privacy, the button reading **Download all data**.
how: Open Settings and choose Data & privacy.
Tap **Download all data**.
The file lands in your downloads, named after your school and today's date.
Open it in any spreadsheet app to sort, filter or share it.
handbook.note: It is a snapshot of the moment you press the button, not a live link. Download it again whenever you need current figures.

handbook.title: Email someone their invite again
handbook.what: Sending the same invite email a second time to somebody who never found the first one. Nothing changes and no new link is made, so the one they may yet dig out of a spam folder still works.
handbook.where: The node's home page, the **Ways in** section, **Email again** on their row. Tap **Show all** first if the ledger is folded.
how: Scroll to **Ways in** on the node's home page.
Find the person's row.
Tap **Email again**.
The note above the table names the address it went to.
handbook.note: Only rows for a named person with an email on file carry this button. If our mail is being eaten by their school's gateway, read them the link instead of sending it a third time.

handbook.title: Export your class list
handbook.what: Taking the class list away as a spreadsheet, with the name, language, belt, journey in phrases, minutes in the app this week, sessions and join code for every class.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the **Export CSV** button along the top.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Filter the list down first if you only want part of it.
Tap **Export CSV**.
The file downloads with today's date in its name.
handbook.note: What you export is what you can see, so a filter applied to the table applies to the file as well.

handbook.title: Find a class in a long list
handbook.what: Narrowing a long list down to the classes you care about right now, by language, and putting them in the order that answers your question.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the strip of pickers above the table.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Pick a language under **Course** to see only the classes learning it.

The list opens ordered by time in app this week, most first. Change **Sort by** to order by name, by how far through the course each class has got, or by phrases practised. On a phone it is the first control, and the number you sorted by shows beside each class name.
handbook.note: The table shows the first three of whatever the pickers produce; **Show all** under it shows the rest.

handbook.title: Find out which email you are signed in with
handbook.what: Telling you which email address this account uses, so you never have to guess when you sign in on another device or ask us for help.
handbook.where: **Settings**, at the top of **Account**.
how: Open **Settings**.
Read the address under **You are signed in as**. Tap it to copy it.
Under it is your account code. Tap to copy that too, and give it to us if you ever get in touch.
handbook.note: The account code names your account and nothing more. It does not let anybody in, so it is safe to read out or put in a message.

handbook.title: Finding your way around the organisation
handbook.what: A standing map down the side of every level, showing where you are: the levels above you, the level you are on, its neighbours and what sits under it. It never disappears, so you can always tell how deep into the organisation you have gone.
handbook.where: The column on the left of any group, school or class page.
how: Open any level of your organisation.
Read down the map to see the path from your top level to here.
Tap any name in it to move straight there.
The page rebuilds around the new level and the map redraws with it.
handbook.note: A leader only ever sees their own part of the organisation — the map is trimmed by the server, not hidden in the page.

handbook.title: Give a class its course
handbook.what: Picking the language a class is learning. This is how a course reaches learners at all — a course does not belong to a person, it belongs to a class, and everybody in that class practises it.
handbook.where: On each class row, the course picker beside the class name. It already holds the language you chose when you signed your school up, so most classes need nothing done here.
how: Leave it as it is to teach the language you signed up with.
To teach something else, tap the picker on the class row.
Start typing a language to narrow the list — the catalogue runs to dozens of courses.
Pick the one you want. Where a language offers more than one version, the versions differ by region or accent.
Save the class, and everyone who joins it lands in that course.
handbook.note: The list here is whatever you left ticked at the Choose courses step. If a course you expect is missing, go back a step and tick it.

handbook.title: Give a teacher their classes
handbook.what: Putting a teacher onto the classes they will teach, working from your staff list rather than opening each class in turn. This is how a new arrival gets their timetable in one sitting.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, the **Assign to a class** button on that teacher's row.
how: Find the teacher in the list.
Tap **Assign to a class**.
Tick every class they should teach.
Tap **Save** to apply the ticks.
handbook.note: This is also how somebody becomes part of your school. Anyone who used your invite link arrives under **Not yet given classes** and can see no learner at all until you tick a class for them, so a stranger who found the link sits there in plain sight and you can remove them. A class with nobody on it says so in the list, and the teacher you tick will lead it. Tick a class that already has a teacher and yours joins as a co-teacher instead.

handbook.title: Hand a class over to another teacher
handbook.what: Passing the lead of a class to another teacher who already teaches it — for a maternity cover, a term swap, or a permanent handover.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Teachers** section.
how: Open the class from My Classes.
Scroll to **Teachers**.
Find the colleague who should lead it.
Tap **Make lead** on their row.
handbook.note: You stay on the class as a teacher. Only the lead changes.

handbook.title: Hand a teacher their access code
handbook.what: A way to get a teacher into their own account when email is not reaching them. School mail gateways quarantine our sign-in codes often enough that this is the rescue, not the exception.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, the **Access code** button on that teacher's row.
how: Find the teacher in the list.
Tap **Access code** on their row.
Read the code out to them, write it down, or paste the link into whatever you already use.
They go to saysomethingin.app/join and type the code in.
Tap **Done** when they are through.
handbook.note: The code works once and lasts two days, and whoever uses it becomes that teacher — so give it to them directly and never post it anywhere shared. Need another? Tap **Access code** again, and the earlier one stops working. This is also how you reissue a code for somebody you added by name who never used the first one.

handbook.title: Hand out a sign-up link for one course
handbook.what: Giving one group of learners a sign-up link that puts them straight into a named course, when your funded year covers more than one. A North Wales tutor hands out the North Welsh link and nobody in that room is asked which Welsh they meant.
handbook.where: The node's home page, the **Ways in** section, the course-named buttons on your sign-up link's row. Tap **Show all** first if the ledger is folded.
how: Scroll to **Ways in** on the node's home page.
Find the row for your sign-up link.
Tap the button named after the course you want, and it is copied.
Send that link to the learners who want that course.
handbook.note: It is the same link and the same cohort either way — the course name only decides where a learner lands. **Copy** still gives you the link that asks them to choose, and everyone gets the whole free year whichever link they came through.

handbook.title: Hand out your staff links
handbook.what: Getting your colleagues in. Your school has a standing teacher link and a standing admin link — send either one and whoever opens it is signed in with that role, with no sign-up form to fill in.
handbook.where: Step two of first-time setup, under **Add your teachers**. The full links are shown as text with a copy button beside each.
how: Open step two of first-time setup.
Copy the **Teacher invite link** for anyone who will run classes.
Copy the **Admin invite link** for anyone who needs to manage the school itself.
Send them however you normally reach staff — email, Teams, a message, or written down.
Anyone who has already joined is listed underneath, so you can see who is in.
handbook.note: A teacher does not need to speak the language. The app does the teaching, so anyone on your staff can run a class.

handbook.title: How every question page is laid out
handbook.what: Every one of the ten questions is answered on a page with the same five parts in the same order, so once you can read one you can read them all: where you are, the answer, the evidence, the rows, and the verbs.
handbook.where: Any page under What's happening.
how: Read the map on the left to see who the question is being asked about.
Read the answer: one plain sentence and one number, with when it was fetched and who is counted directly beneath.
Read the evidence: one chart, never two side by side.
Open any row beneath it. Every row is a link to the thing it names.
The buttons across the top of the main column are the things you can do about the answer. When there is nothing to do, the strip is empty rather than missing.
handbook.note: No page may add a part or move one. A page that tried to would fail the build.

handbook.title: How far a class has travelled
handbook.what: A bar showing where a class has got to in its course, measured in phrases — the individual pieces of language the course teaches. A class is one learner account played from the front, so the position is the class's own.
handbook.where: The **Course journey** card on a class page.
how: Open a class.
Read the bar for how much of the course the class has covered together.
The line underneath gives the figure in phrases, then names the next belt and how many phrases are left to reach it.
handbook.note: A class that has never played together says **Not started** in words; it is never shown as a bar of zero.

handbook.title: How fresh these numbers are
handbook.what: A small time stamp saying when the figures on the page were last loaded, so you always know whether you are looking at this morning or this minute.
handbook.where: Just above the row of numbers, reading **Updated** and a time.
how: Open any level of your organisation.
Read the stamp above the numbers for the time they were fetched.
Pull the page down or reload it to fetch again — the stamp moves with it.
handbook.note: Nothing is shown until the first load has genuinely succeeded, so an empty stamp means the numbers have not arrived rather than that they are old.

handbook.title: How many in-app minutes are being done
handbook.what: The first question: how many in-app minutes are being done, per course, in total and per person on the course, and how each course stands against the average of all courses. A minute is everything between pressing play and stopping, on every screen, and Listening Mode minutes are shown apart from main-flow minutes. The average of all courses is the same number whichever course you pick: it counts this course too, and for the per-person and no-activity measures it is worked out over every person on every course, so a course with two enrolments weighs two people, not a whole course.
handbook.where: **Minutes**, the first question in the bar, and where Intelligence opens.
how: Pick the **window**: today, the last seven days or the last thirty days.
Pick the **course**. It opens on the busiest course in that window.
Pick the **measure**: minutes per person, minutes in total, new enrolments, or people with no activity. The line under the pickers says what it counts and what the average of all courses is for it.
Read the two numbers: this course against the average of all courses, and the strip beneath for where the course sits among the rest.
Read the line under the strip for the split between the main flow and Listening Mode, and how many people the minutes are spread over.
The rows further down still count the real people who practised this week, by course; open one to see which bits of the course give trouble.
handbook.note: Every minute here is the same minute every school page shows, and a person on the course who did not press play still counts in the denominator.

handbook.title: How students join a class
handbook.what: The one door into a class. A student who follows the class link signs up and lands straight in the class, on the right course, with no code to type. The same class also has a short code for a room where a link is awkward.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Invite students** card.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Copy the link from the **Invite students** card and send it to your students.
For a room with a whiteboard, tap **Show code instead** and write the code up.
Students enter that code at saysomethingin.com/redeem.
handbook.note: The link and the code both stay valid, so the same one works for a student who joins in week one and a student who arrives in week six. If the card says it could not load, do not hand anything out until it comes back.

handbook.title: Invite a teacher to your school
handbook.what: One standing link that turns anyone who opens it into a teacher of your school. It is the same link every time, so you can hand it to a whole staff room at once.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, the **Invite teachers** card below the list.
how: Open **Teachers**.
Scroll to the **Invite teachers** card.
Tap **Copy invite link**.
Send it however you reach your staff — Teams, WhatsApp, printed on a slip.
They open it, sign in once, and appear in your list as a teacher.
handbook.note: If you are standing in front of them rather than sending anything, **Show code instead** gives you a short code to read out or write on a whiteboard, and they type it in at saysomethingin.com/redeem.

handbook.title: Invite a teacher who isn't here yet
handbook.what: Getting a teacher who has no account yet into one class of yours, without going through the school admin.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Teachers** section.
how: Open the class from My Classes.
Scroll to **Teachers**.
Take the co-teacher link.
Send it to them — opening it puts them on this class as a teacher.
handbook.note: The link is scoped to this one class, so a cover teacher never lands in the rest of the school.

handbook.title: Let a named address in through your links
handbook.what: Marking one named person as expected when their email is not at your school's domain: a supply teacher here for a fortnight, or a colleague who only uses a personal address. It stops them being sorted to the top of **Not yet given classes** as somebody you might not know.
handbook.where: Settings, the **Which addresses look like your school** card, the **Add address** field.
how: Open Settings and find **Which addresses look like your school**.
Type their email address exactly as they will use it.
Tap **Add address**, then send them your usual teacher link.
handbook.note: They get in with one tap either way, with or without this. What actually puts somebody in your school is giving them a class. If you know who they are before they arrive, **Add by name** on the Teachers page is the shorter route.

handbook.title: Look up one student
handbook.what: Finding one learner among all of them and opening what they have actually done. The list carries their belt, their hours this week, and when they were last here, so you can often answer the question without opening anything.
handbook.where: The **Students** page, the search box and filters above the list, then **View** on their row.
how: Open **Students**.
Type part of their name in the search box, or narrow the list by class or belt.
Read their row for belt, hours and last active.
Tap **View** to open their own progress.
handbook.note: The row records what the learner has done and when they were last here. It makes no judgement about how they are doing.

handbook.title: Make a class
handbook.what: Setting up a class of your own: a name, a language, and a link students use to join it. A class holds a roster, its own place on the course, and everything the class practises together.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the **+ New class** button along the top of the page.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Tap **+ New class**.
Give the class a name you will recognise on a list, such as Year 7 Welsh.
Choose the language the class is learning.
Tap **Create Class**.
handbook.note: The join link is made for you at the same moment. Nothing else is needed to start teaching.

handbook.title: Make a link anyone can use
handbook.what: One link, by role, that you can put in a newsletter or on a slide and let a whole room use. Unlike a personal invite it is not tied to anybody, so new arrivals type their own name before they are in.
handbook.where: The node's home page, **Get a shareable link** along the top.
how: Open the home page of the group, school or organisation they should join.
Tap **Get a shareable link**.
Pick the role everyone using it will arrive as.
Tap **Create invite link** and copy what comes back.
handbook.note: It is open to anyone holding it, so when a link has travelled further than you meant, revoke it in **Ways in** and make a fresh one. Use **Invite a person** instead when you can name who is coming.

handbook.title: Manage a class
handbook.what: Getting from the class page to the class's tools: the roster of pupils on their own accounts, the teachers, the join link and code, renaming and deleting.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Manage class** link beside the class name.
how: Open the class.
Tap **Manage class**.
The tools page opens; its own **Open the class page** line brings you back.
handbook.note: The class's practice, minutes and journey stay on the class page. The tools page never totals whole-class play.

handbook.title: Minutes in the app this week
handbook.what: How much your school practised this week, in minutes: the time your classes spent in the app with a lesson running, pauses included, plus any teacher or pupil practising on their own account, each counted once. Under it, how many of your classes practised at all this week.
handbook.where: The stat strip at the top of the schools dashboard.
how: Read the number. It is minutes, never hours, and it is this week only.
Read the line beneath it for how many classes practised.
handbook.note: A dash means this week's figures have not loaded — pull to refresh. It is never shown as a zero that is not real.

handbook.title: Move a teacher to another class
handbook.what: Changing which classes a teacher is on, in one pass, without visiting each class in turn.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Teachers** section, a teacher's other classes.
how: Open a class the teacher is on.
Scroll to **Teachers** and open their other classes.
Tick the classes they should be on and untick the ones they should not.
Save.
handbook.note: Untick and save is how you take a teacher off a class — there is no separate remove.

handbook.title: Name your school
handbook.what: Telling the app what your school is actually called. The name you type here is the one your teachers and students see on every page, on every invite link they open, and at the top of every report.
handbook.where: Step one of first-time setup, the box marked **School name**.
how: Open first-time setup and stay on step one.
Type your school's name as you would write it on a letterhead.
Tap **Continue** — the name is saved before the next step opens.
If you have just arrived and the box is empty for a second, give it a moment and press **Continue** again.
handbook.note: Typing it here counts as confirming it, so you will not be asked to confirm your school's name again afterwards. To change it later, use School profile in Settings.

handbook.title: One person's story
handbook.what: Everything that answers a support call about one person: who they are, their support id, whether they count as a real person, what they can play and through which door, where they are in each course, what they did last and on what.
handbook.where: **One person**, under What's happening. Open a row on Leaving, or find them under People.
how: Read the sentence for their standing, their access and their last practice, and the pill beneath it for whether they count.

Use the verbs across the top to act: give full access, take it back, make a one-off sign-in link, change their role, change their trial, or correct a wrong flag. Every verb says what it will change and asks before it does.
Read the cards for their access, their memberships, their course positions and their last few events.
handbook.note: Every verb is recorded against your own name by the server. A comped person stays a real person; only staff and test are left out of the numbers.

handbook.title: Open a class
handbook.what: Going from the summary row into the class itself. A school leader lands on the class's own page: what it practised this week, its minutes in the app, how far it has travelled and who teaches it, with **Invite students** and **See insights** at the top. A teacher lands on the class tools: the roster, the teachers, the join link and the class's progress.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, anywhere on the class's row.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Tap the row for the class you want.
The class page opens.
handbook.note: The row is a button in its own right, so a keyboard works too. The buttons at the right of the row do their own jobs and do not open the class.

handbook.title: Open the folded ledger
handbook.what: Turning the one-row-per-role summary of your links into the full ledger, where every link has its own row and its own verbs.
handbook.where: The **Ways in** section, the **Show all** line under the role rows. It only appears when there are more than three links.
how: Scroll to **Ways in** on the node's home page.
Tap **Show all**.
The ledger opens with its filter chips and every link's row.
Tap **Show fewer** at the bottom to fold it back.
handbook.note: Nothing is ever hidden for good: every link is one tap away.

handbook.title: Open your inbox
handbook.what: Getting to the messages sent to you: a reply on your Support thread, or a notice that your own practice was copied onto a class account. The dot on your avatar and the number beside **Inbox** are how many you have not opened.
handbook.where: **Inbox** in the account menu at the top right, under your name, just above Support.
how: Tap your name at the top right.
Tap **Inbox**.
handbook.note: The number only goes down when you open a message, not when it arrives. The item is not shown while a platform admin is viewing the dashboard as someone else.

handbook.title: Play as class from the class page
handbook.what: Starting a whole-class lesson from the class's own page, on the class's own account, so the minutes and the phrases land on the class rather than on you.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Play as class** button beside the class name.
how: Open the class from your dashboard or from My Classes.
Tap **Play as class**.
The player opens on the class's course at the class's own place.
handbook.note: Pressing play on a course from your own Library counts for you, not for the class. Only Play as class moves the class. While a platform admin is viewing the page as you the button is greyed out and does nothing.

handbook.title: Play as class from your dashboard
handbook.what: Starting a whole-class lesson straight from your dashboard, on the class's own account, so the minutes and the phrases land on the class rather than on you.
handbook.where: Your dashboard, the **Play as class** button on each class's card or row.
how: Find the class on your dashboard.
Tap **Play as class**.
The player opens on the class's course at the class's own place.
handbook.note: The button is always there beside the class. While a platform admin is viewing the dashboard as you it is greyed out and does nothing, so they can see what you have without starting a lesson in your name.

handbook.title: Practice on your own account
handbook.what: Telling you when practice this week landed on your own sign-in rather than on a class. Pressing play on a course from your Library counts for you; only Play as class counts for the class. The line names your own minutes and when you last played, so a lesson that went to the wrong place is found rather than lost.
handbook.where: Under your classes on the schools dashboard, only in a week when your own account has practised.
how: Read the line.
Next lesson, tap **Play as class** on the class instead of playing from the Library.
To move this week's lesson onto the class, open the class and use **Ran a lesson signed in as yourself?** on its tools page.
handbook.note: The line never appears when your own account is quiet, so its absence means nothing went astray.

handbook.title: Prove your mailbox reaches you
handbook.what: School mail gateways are ferocious, and a code that never arrives is only discovered on the day you need it. This asks once, at the moment you have just made something worth keeping, and settles it.
handbook.where: A card that appears right after you create a class or copy a class join link, for as long as your address is unproven.
how: Tap **Send me a code**, or nominate a different address if your school one eats our mail.
Type the six digits we send, and tap **That's the one**.
handbook.note: Close it and it stays closed. It never comes back on a timer.

handbook.title: Put the app on your device
handbook.what: Putting SSi on your phone or tablet as an app, so it opens from the home screen and works without a browser tab.
handbook.where: Your node's home page, **Your account**.
how: Open your home page on the device you want it on.
Scroll to **Your account**.
Tap the install row and follow the prompt your device gives you.
handbook.note: Install it on the device you actually teach from — the install belongs to the device, not to your account.

handbook.title: Read your class list
handbook.what: One row per class, showing at a glance what each one has done. A class is one learner account, played from the front of the room, so every figure on the row is that account's own: the belt the class has reached, how far through the course it has travelled in phrases, minutes played as class over the last seven days and the shape of those days. Nothing on the row grades the class. Played as class is time with the lesson running on the class account, from pressing play to stopping, pauses included — the same minute the class page, the school home and Insights count. Pupils' own practice is not in it. A class that has never played says **Not started** in words rather than showing a row of zeros.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the table filling most of the page. On a phone each class is a card instead, with the number you sorted by beside its name and the rest underneath.
how: Open **My Classes**.
The first three classes show; tap **Show all** under the table for the rest, and **Show fewer** to fold them back.
Read down the time in app column first, because minutes in the lesson are the figure the school runs on.
Use the small chart in each row to see whether practice is steady or has stopped.
Compare time in the app this week between classes taking the same course.
handbook.note: A quiet week shows as low minutes and a flat chart, nothing more. The app makes no judgement about how a class is doing.

handbook.title: Read your messages
handbook.what: Reading what has been sent to you: a reply on your Support thread, or a notice that your own practice was copied onto a class account, with one tap to undo it.
handbook.where: **Inbox** in the account menu at the top right, under your name. The number beside it is how many you have not opened.
how: Tap your name at the top right, then **Inbox**.
Tap a message to open it. Opening it is what marks it read.
If the message offers **Undo** or **Open Support**, tap that.
handbook.note: A message stays unread until you open it, even after it has been on the list a while. Undo is offered only while it can be done cleanly; once the class account has been played since, it is not.

handbook.title: Reading one student's progress
handbook.what: Every student in a class, one to a row, each carrying their own position in the course, their belt, their practice over the last week and how recently they were active. A quiet coloured dot flags anyone who has gone quiet or fallen well behind the class.
handbook.where: The **Students on their own accounts** list at the bottom of a class page. It is only there when at least one pupil has an account of their own.
how: Open a class.
Read down the rows — the bar on each is that student's own position in the course, in phrases. The first three show; tap **Show all** under them for the rest.
The small chart beside it is their practice over the past week, with the minutes named.
The dot and word at the start of a row say whether they are excellent, good, needing attention or inactive.
Tap a row to open that person.
handbook.note: Needing attention means either nothing for a fortnight or less than half the class average, so it is a prompt to look rather than a verdict.

handbook.title: Reading your insights
handbook.what: Reading the pace of learning at this level — what is being counted, over what period, and against what.
handbook.where: The node's home page, **See insights**.
how: Open the node's home page and tap **See insights**.
Pick the **measure** — rate of progress, practice minutes, or active classes. The line underneath says exactly what it means.

Pick the **window** — the period the figure covers. A wider window never reads less practice than a narrower one, because practice minutes are the total inside the window, from pressing play to stopping.
Use **Compare to** to put an average alongside.
**Overview** takes you back to the same place's home page.
handbook.note: Rate of progress is a per-week rate; practice minutes is a plain total. The chart is one bar per day, hour or month, and a bar with no play is a zero. A class that practises from the front is counted through its own class account, so whole-class lessons show here the same as any other practice.

handbook.title: Remove a student from a class
handbook.what: Taking a student off a class roster, for a pupil who has changed set or joined the wrong class from a shared link.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Remove** button at the end of the student's row in the roster.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Find the student in the roster.
Tap **Remove** at the end of their row.
Confirm when asked.
handbook.note: The student keeps their account and everything they have learned, and they can join another class straight away. Only their place on this roster goes.

handbook.title: Remove a teacher from your school
handbook.what: Taking a teacher off your school when they leave. Their own account survives — what goes is their place in this school and their view of its classes and learners. It is also how you deal with somebody under **Not yet given classes** you do not recognise, or a name you typed by mistake.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, the **Remove** button on that teacher's row.
how: Find the teacher in the list.
Tap **Remove** on their row.
Confirm when asked for their name back.
The list refreshes without them.
handbook.note: An admin's row carries no **Remove** button, so a school can never lose its own admin through this list. Change their role first if that is really what you want.

handbook.title: Rename a class
handbook.what: Changing what a class is called, for a name typed in a hurry or a group that has moved up a year.
handbook.where: The class page, the small pencil beside the class name.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Tap the pencil next to the name at the top.
Type the new name.
Confirm it.
handbook.note: Only the name changes. The roster, the join link, the join code and the class's place on the course all carry on exactly as they were.

handbook.title: Rename a school or group
handbook.what: Changing what a school or group is called everywhere it appears. Nothing else moves — the same people, classes and links carry on under the new name.
handbook.where: The node's home page, **Rename** along the top.
how: Open the home page of the school or group.
Tap **Rename**.
Type the new name.
Tap **Save**.
handbook.note: If the new name matches something else already sitting beside it you are warned and asked to confirm, because two identical names in one list is usually a mistake rather than a plan.

handbook.title: Report a bug from Settings
handbook.what: Opening the report sheet when something in the app has gone wrong.
handbook.where: **Settings**, under **Tools**, the **Report a bug** row.
how: Open **Settings**.
Tap **Report a bug**.
Describe what happened on the sheet that opens and tap **Send**.
handbook.note: The row is there whether or not you are signed in. What you send goes to one place and nobody replies through the app.

handbook.title: Report a bug from the dashboard
handbook.what: Telling us when the dashboard misbehaves, or suggesting something, without leaving the dashboard. The page you are on and your school are attached for you.
handbook.where: **Report a bug** in the account menu at the top right, under your name.
how: Tap your name at the top right, then **Report a bug**.
Write what happened, add a screenshot if you have one, and tap **Send**.
handbook.note: Nobody replies through the app: the note goes to one place where we read it. Questions about the dashboard go to **Support** instead. The item is not shown while a platform admin is viewing the dashboard as someone else.

handbook.title: Run your first class session
handbook.what: Running a live practice session with a class in the room, everyone hearing the same thing at the same time.
handbook.where: The class page, the join link and the play button.
how: Open the class from My Classes.
Put the join link or the join code on the screen for the room.
Wait for the students to arrive on their own devices.
Tap play to start the session.
handbook.note: The join code is the same code all lesson, so a student arriving late still gets in. While a platform admin is viewing the page as you the play button is greyed out and does nothing.

handbook.title: Say what happened
handbook.what: The box where you describe the problem in your own words.
handbook.where: The **What happened?** box on the report sheet.
how: Tap into the box and write what you saw.
Keep it under 2,000 characters. Send stays off until you have written something.
handbook.note: Your course and device details are added for you, so you only need to describe what went wrong.

handbook.title: Say what happened on the dashboard
handbook.what: The box where you describe the bug, or the thing you would like, in your own words.
handbook.where: The **What happened?** box on the Report a bug window that opens from the account menu.
how: Tap into the box and write what you saw.
Keep it under 2,000 characters. Send stays off until you have written something.
handbook.note: The page you were on, your school, your role and your account are added for you, so you only need to describe what went wrong.

handbook.title: See and download your funder numbers
handbook.what: The monthly return your funder asks for, on your own page, so you can read it or send it without asking us to pull it.
handbook.where: Your organisation's home page, the **Funder report** section.
how: Open your organisation's home page.
The month shown is the last complete one. Change it to report on another.
Read the three blocks: the month, everything since people enrolled, and the funding year so far.
Tap **Download spreadsheet** to get the same figures as a CSV.
handbook.note: Minutes here are minutes the app was actually speaking to a learner, never time a screen sat open. Somebody who has studied both Welsh dialects is counted once, at their higher dialect, never the two added up. There are no names in this report and there never will be — the age question is a tick precisely so nobody has to hold a birth date.

handbook.title: See every school in your programme
handbook.what: One table of every school you look after, with its students, teachers, classes and practice hours side by side, so a whole programme reads at a glance instead of school by school.
handbook.where: All schools. The totals sit above the table and the search and sort controls sit on its header row.
how: Open All schools.
Read the totals across the top for the programme as a whole.
Search by name to find one school, or sort by name, hours or students.
Read the Status column — a school with nobody running it yet is flagged as awaiting admin.
Tap any row to open that school's own dashboard.
Tap **Export** for the same table as a spreadsheet file.
handbook.note: The list holds still until you refresh it, so a number on screen will not change under you while you are reading. If a refresh fails you are told plainly rather than being shown stale figures as if they were current.

handbook.title: See that your report arrived
handbook.what: Confirming the note reached us.
handbook.where: The **Got it, thank you** line that replaces the form once it has sent.
how: Tap **Send** on the report sheet.
Read **Got it, thank you**. The sheet closes on its own a moment later, or tap the line to close it now.
handbook.note: That line is the whole reply. There is no ticket number and no message back.

handbook.title: See what a funded organisation gives its learners
handbook.what: Showing the courses an organisation hands out through its own sign-up page, which are given to each learner as they join rather than held on the organisation itself.
handbook.where: The organisation's home page, **Courses** along the top, at the head of the panel.
how: Open the organisation's home page.
Tap **Courses**.
Read the courses listed under the organisation's name, and the length of the free period beside them.
handbook.note: Changing that list is a change to the organisation's enrolment policy, so it is not editable here — everyone who has already signed up keeps what they were given.

handbook.title: See what your school pays
handbook.what: The plain statement of your school's plan — its name, how many teacher seats it is paying for, and whether the subscription is live.
handbook.where: Settings, then Billing.
how: Open Settings and choose Billing.
Read the current plan line: your school, its seat count, and active if the subscription is running.
Tap **Manage subscription & seats** to change how many seats you pay for.
Tap **Billing & invoices** to reach invoices, change the card, or cancel.
handbook.note: Every payment change happens on the one Upgrade page, so there is a single place to go and no second checkout to get confused with. The invoices button appears once a subscription is running.

handbook.title: Send a dashboard bug report
handbook.what: Sending your note, and your screenshot if you added one, to us.
handbook.where: The **Send** button at the foot of the Report a bug window.
how: Write what happened, and what you expected if that helps.
Tap **Send**. It reads **Sending…** while it goes.
handbook.note: A **Got it, thank you** line appears at the top of the page and that is the whole reply. Nobody answers through the app. If the screenshot cannot upload, the note still goes without it.

handbook.title: Send the report
handbook.what: Sending your note, and your screenshot if you added one, to us.
handbook.where: The **Send** button at the foot of the report sheet.
how: Write what happened.
Tap **Send**. It reads **Sending…** while it goes.
handbook.note: If the screenshot cannot upload, the note still goes without it. If the note itself does not send, the sheet says so and you can tap Send again.

handbook.title: Set or change your password
handbook.what: Giving yourself a password so you can sign back in without waiting for a link in your email.
handbook.where: Your node's home page, **Your account**.
how: Open your home page and scroll to **Your account**.
Tap the password row.
Type the password you want and save.
handbook.note: Your original invite link keeps working. A password is a second door, not a replacement.

handbook.title: Set up a demo organisation
handbook.what: Standing up a whole organisation with plausible people and activity already in it, for showing somebody what the product looks like once it is running rather than what it looks like empty.
handbook.where: The home page of the node it should sit under, **Mint a demo org** along the top.
how: Open the home page of the node the demo belongs under.
Tap **Mint a demo org**.
Type a name for it, and a leader's email if somebody is to be handed it.
Tap **Mint**, and copy the leader link that comes back.
handbook.note: A demo org's own page grows a **Refresh demo activity** button, which moves its learners on so a demo you minted weeks ago does not look abandoned when you next open it.

handbook.title: Set your language and time zone
handbook.what: Choosing the language the dashboard itself speaks to you in, and the time zone your dates and times are read against.
handbook.where: Settings, then Localisation.
how: Open Settings and choose Localisation.
Pick a **Default interface language**.
Pick a **Time zone** so activity times read correctly for where you are.
Tap **Save changes**.
handbook.note: This is remembered on the device you set it on. Teachers and students each choose their own, so setting it here does not change what anybody else sees.

handbook.title: Share a class with a colleague
handbook.what: Adding another teacher to a class you already run, so you both see the same roster and the same progress.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Teachers** section.
how: Open the class from My Classes.
Scroll to **Teachers**.
Tap **Add a teacher**.
Pick your colleague from the list.
handbook.note: Both of you are teachers of the class. One of you is the lead, and the lead is the one the school's lists show first.

handbook.title: Start a class session from the list
handbook.what: Starting a shared practice session for a class without opening the class first. Your device leads and the whole class moves together from where the class last got to.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the **Play as class** button at the end of the class's row.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Find the class you are about to teach.
Tap **Play as class** at the end of its row.
The player opens on that class's course, at the class's own place in it.
handbook.note: It is the same session the class page starts, so it moves the class on for everyone on the roster. Only school staff see this button. While a platform admin is viewing the dashboard as you it is greyed out and does nothing, so they can see what you have without starting a lesson in your name.

handbook.title: Students on their own accounts
handbook.what: The pupils who have signed in on their own account and joined this class, one row each, with their belt, how much they have learned, how much they have practised on that account and when they were last at it. It counts only what each pupil did signed in as themselves. Whole-class play from the front is not in this table; that is on the class page.
handbook.where: The class tools page, the **Students on their own accounts** table.
how: Open **Manage class** from the class page.
Read down the rows for who is practising on their own and who has gone quiet.
Type a name into the search box to jump to one student.
handbook.note: A class taught from the front with no pupil accounts has nobody in this table, and that is not a class that has done nothing. A student who has never started shows as inactive rather than as behind. A class nobody has joined yet shows **Add students** and points at the invite link instead of an empty table.

handbook.title: Subscribe as a tutor
handbook.what: Paying for your own tutoring dashboard when you teach on your own rather than inside a school. It is one seat, for you.
handbook.where: The **Upgrade** button on your tutoring dashboard.
how: Open the Upgrade page.
Choose Monthly or Annual — annual works out at two months free.
Tap **Subscribe** and fill in the card details on the payment panel that opens on the page.
Once it is running, the same button becomes **Manage subscription** for invoices and cancellation.
handbook.note: Your students pay for their own learning separately, so three paying students cover what your dashboard costs.

handbook.title: Subscribe your organisation
handbook.what: Putting your whole organisation on a paid plan. You pay per learner seat, and one subscription covers every seat and every language across the group.
handbook.where: The **Upgrade** button on your organisation's dashboard.
how: Open the Upgrade page.
Choose Monthly or Annual — annual works out at two months free per seat.
Set the number of learner seats with the stepper. It opens at the number of people already joined.
Tap **Subscribe** and fill in the card details on the payment panel that opens on the page.
handbook.note: A seat belongs to one named learner for the whole period you have paid for, so plan the count against the people you expect rather than swapping seats between them mid-term. You can add more seats at any time.

handbook.title: Subscribe your school
handbook.what: Turning a trial into a paid school. You pay per teacher seat, and one subscription covers every language and every class those teachers run.
handbook.where: The **Upgrade** button on your dashboard, or Settings then Billing then **Subscribe / choose seats**.
how: Open the Upgrade page.
Choose Monthly or Annual — annual works out at two months free per seat.
Set the number of teacher seats with the stepper. It opens at the number of teachers who have actually joined.
Tap **Subscribe** and fill in the card details on the payment panel that opens on the page.
You come back to the dashboard with the subscription live.
handbook.note: Seats are teacher seats, not student seats. Your students do not each need one.

handbook.title: Take a domain or address off your school's list
handbook.what: Taking a domain or a named address off the list your Teachers page sorts by.
handbook.where: Settings, the **Which addresses look like your school** card, the **Remove** button beside the entry.
how: Open Settings and find **Which addresses look like your school**.
Tap **Remove** beside the domain or address.
handbook.note: Nobody loses anything and nobody is kept out. Arrivals from that address simply stop being sorted to the bottom of **Not yet given classes**.

handbook.title: Take a teacher off a class, or move them
handbook.what: Changing which classes a teacher takes without removing them from the school. The ticks start from what is true today, so moving somebody from one class to another is a single change rather than two.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, **Assign to a class** on that teacher's row, then the ticks.
how: Open **Assign to a class** on the teacher's row.
Untick the class they are leaving.
Tick the class they are joining, if there is one.
Tap **Save** — the button counts your changes back to you before you commit.
handbook.note: If part of a change fails the panel stays open and names the class it could not do, and the ticks reset to what is actually true. Nothing is ever reported as saved when it was not.

handbook.title: Take your lists away as a spreadsheet
handbook.what: A CSV of whoever is currently on screen, for a report, a governors' meeting, or your own sums in a spreadsheet.
handbook.where: The **Students** page and the **Teachers** page, **Export CSV** along the top.
how: Filter or search the list down to whoever you want.
Tap **Export CSV**.
The file downloads with today's date in its name.
Open it in whatever spreadsheet you use.
handbook.note: The export follows your filters, not the whole school — so a filtered list gives you a filtered file. Clear the filters first if you want everybody.

handbook.title: Tell us about something that went wrong
handbook.what: Sending us a note when the app misbehaves, with the details of your course and device attached for you.
handbook.where: The sheet that opens from **Report a bug** in **Settings**.
how: Tap **Report a bug** in Settings.
Write what happened, add a screenshot if you have one, and tap **Send**.
handbook.note: Tapping outside the sheet closes it without sending. Nobody replies through the app: the note goes to one place where we read it.

handbook.title: The classes by year group
handbook.what: A row of small tiles under the page head, one per year group, each headed by its year, **Y7**, **Y8** and so on: the minutes that year's classes spent in the app this week and how many of them practised out of how many there are. It says in one glance which years are the school's engine and which have barely started.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the **By year group** card under the page head, once this week's practice has loaded.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Find the year by its big label on each tile.
Read the minutes under it for time in the app this week. It is the same minute as the page head and the class rows, added up across that year's classes.
Read the line under that for classes practising out of classes in that year.
Tap a tile and the table below narrows to that year's classes; a **Year 7 ×** chip in the pickers takes the filter off again.
A tile reading **Other** holds the classes whose names carry no year.
handbook.note: The year is read off the class name — a leading number from 6 to 13, so **7B**, **Year 9 French** and **10 Set 1** all count — and is never stored. A dash means no minutes this week. If fewer than half your class names carry a year the card reads **By class** instead, most minutes first, three then **Show all**, and each of those tiles opens its class.

handbook.title: The invites desk
handbook.what: The platform-wide desk where SSi mints and manages invites across every organisation at once.
handbook.where: The admin area, **Invites**.
how: Open the invites desk from the admin area.
Pick the mode from the strip along the top — the mode decides what kind of invite you are minting.
Fill in who it is for and submit.
Use the active toggle to read live invites rather than spent ones.
handbook.note: This is the operator's desk, not a school's. A school brings its own people in from its own home page.

handbook.title: The numbers by year group
handbook.what: The row of small tiles under the numbers, one per year group, so a head can see at a glance which years are doing it and which have barely started. Each tile is headed by its year, **Y7**, **Y8** and so on, with the minutes that year's classes spent in the app this week beneath it and how many of its classes practised out of how many there are.
handbook.where: The **By year group** card directly under the row of numbers on a school or group page.
how: Open a school or a group.
Find the year by its big label on each tile.
Read the minutes under it for time in the app this week, the same minute the numbers above and the class rows count.
Read the line under that for classes practising out of classes in that year.
A tile reading **Other** holds the classes whose names carry no year.
On your own school, tap a tile to open the classes list narrowed to that year's classes.
handbook.note: The year is read off the class name — a leading number from 6 to 13, so **7B**, **Year 9 French** and **10 Set 1** all count — and is never stored. A dash means no minutes this week. If fewer than half your class names carry a year the card reads **By class** instead, most minutes first, three then **Show all**, and each of those tiles opens its class.

handbook.title: The numbers on any level
handbook.what: The row of figures at the top of any level of your organisation. They always count everything below that level, each person once, so a group's numbers already include every school, class and learner underneath it.
handbook.where: Across the top of the page for a group, a school or a class, under the name.
how: Open the level you want — a group, a school or a class.

**Phrases practised this week** is how many phrases the classes beneath this level were prompted with in whole-class play over the last seven days. It is recorded as each phrase's turn begins, so it counts every phrase the lesson reached.
**Classes practising this week** is how many of them played together in the last seven days, out of all the classes below.

**Minutes in the app this week** is the time the classes beneath this level, and their staff and students on their own accounts, spent in the app over the last seven days, pauses included — the time they were in the lesson. The sentence under the row says how much of it was whole-class play and how much was audio playing.
**Teachers** counts the staff below this level, each once however many classes they take.
On a class the row switches to that class's own phrases practised this week, its minutes in the app, its students and its teachers.

On your own school every card is a link: phrases and minutes open the classes list with the classes in that order, classes practising opens it narrowed to the classes that played this week, and teachers opens the staff list.
handbook.note: An organisation that is not school-shaped sees minutes in the app this week, groups and learners instead. Every minute on this page is the same minute: from pressing play to stopping, over the last seven days, each account once. There is no all-time total here.

handbook.title: Told when you are playing as yourself
handbook.what: A line across the top of the player while a lesson is running on your own sign-in rather than on the class, so it is noticed before the minutes land on you. It reads: You are now playing as yourself. If you want to play as class please go here.
handbook.where: Across the top of the player, only while it is playing on your own account. The player moves down to make room for it, so it covers none of the controls. Your dashboard never shows it: nothing is playing there.
how: Read the line.
Tap **Your classes** to go to your classes, and start the lesson with **Play as class** there.
handbook.note: The line goes as soon as you pause or stop. Minutes already played on your own account are not moved by it; the copy tool on a class's tools page does that if you want it.

handbook.title: Voice and pause
handbook.what: What the microphone is actually giving us below this level: how many learners have any mic-derived data at all, and for those who do, how the pause the app leaves them to speak in is settling, and how they sound when they speak.
handbook.where: The **Voice and pause** section at the bottom of any level's insights page.
how: Open a level and tap **See insights**.
Scroll past the rate comparison to the voice section.
Read the uptake figure first — it is how many learners this is based on.
Open a class or a learner within it to see the same reading at a smaller scope.
handbook.note: A learner with no microphone data is absent from these figures rather than counted as a zero, so the denominator is always stated. A class that practises from the front counts as one learner, its own class account, so a school with no pupil accounts still has a roster here.

handbook.title: Walking down to a school, a class or a person
handbook.what: A drawn tree of everything hanging beneath the level you are on — groups inside groups, the classes in each, the teachers who take them and the staff who teach nothing yet. It is one picture of the shape of your organisation, not a list you have to filter.
handbook.where: The **Below this** panel under the numbers on any group or school page.
how: Open a group or a school.
Tap a caret to open or close what sits under a name.
Tap any name to go to that level — the numbers and the tree redraw for it.

A class row names its teachers, its student count, and how many phrases it practised together in the last seven days, or says plainly that it has not practised together this week, without you opening it.
Where there are more than three groups, classes or people under a name, the first three show and **Show all** reveals the rest; **Show fewer** folds them away again.
handbook.note: The top two levels open themselves and deeper ones wait to be tapped, so a large organisation shows you its shape instead of eighty-five rows.

handbook.title: Ways in — who can get in, and how to change it
handbook.what: The ledger of every way into this part of the tree — who has a live link, what it lets them do, and how to change your mind.
handbook.where: The node's home page, the **Ways in** section below the lists.
how: Open the node's home page and scroll to **Ways in**.

With more than three links, read one row per role — class links, teacher links, leader links — each saying how many there are and how often they have been used. A row with a single link carries **Copy**.
Tap **Show all** to open the full ledger: each row a live way in, personal or shareable, filterable by role and by place with the chips. **Show fewer** folds it back.
**Copy** hands you the link again.
**Re-mint** issues a fresh link and kills the old one on the spot.
**Revoke** closes that way in entirely.
handbook.note: A shareable link is open to anyone who holds it, so revoke is the tool when a link has travelled further than you meant.

handbook.title: What the nightly findings say about this question
handbook.what: Every night a job reads the week's practice and writes a handful of findings in plain words. Each one appears here on the question it is about, so you read the finding beside the number it is a finding about.
handbook.where: The cards between the verbs and the answer on a question page. A question with no findings shows nothing here.
how: Read the cards. Each carries a dot in one of four tones: good, watch, alarm or quiet.
Read the line above them for when they were found.
If that line is red, the nightly job has missed two nights or more and the findings are old. The job is not on this estate and cannot be restarted from here.
handbook.note: The numbers inside a finding were the job's own on the night; the page's own numbers are fetched fresh and may differ.

handbook.title: What your classes actually practised
handbook.what: A list of the phrases the classes beneath this level practised together in the last seven days, with how many times each one came round. A phrase that appears again and again is the course bringing it back on purpose, which is how it sticks.
handbook.where: The **What they practised this week** card under the row of numbers on a group or school page, and on a class page under its own practice card.
how: Open a group, a school or a class.
Read the three rows: the prompt, the phrase the class practised, and the number of times it came round this week. The three most practised come first.
Tap **Show all** under them to see every phrase; **Show fewer** folds the list back.
Tap a column heading to sort by it.
handbook.note: A level whose classes have not played together this week says so in words instead of showing an empty list. Only whole-class play appears here; what staff and students practise on their own accounts is counted in the minutes in the app figure above.

handbook.title: When an answer was fetched
handbook.what: Saying when the numbers on a question page were actually read from the database, so you know whether you are looking at this minute or this morning.
handbook.where: Beneath the answer sentence on every question page, reading **Updated** and a time.
how: Read the time beneath the answer.
While it reads **Updating**, the page is still fetching and no number on it is final.
handbook.note: The time is taken when the fetch completed, never when the page drew itself.

handbook.title: When more people join than you have seats
handbook.what: What happens when your school or organisation outgrows the seats it is paying for. Nothing is blocked, nobody is locked out, and no lesson stops. The page simply tells you the truth so you can put it right.
handbook.where: The Upgrade page, the line directly under the seat stepper.
how: Open the Upgrade page.
Read the line under the stepper: how many people have joined, and how many seats are paid for.
If more have joined than you pay for, the line says so and names the difference.
Step the seat count up to match and tap the update button.
handbook.note: This is deliberately an honest count rather than a gate. We would rather show you the gap than shut a class out mid-lesson.

handbook.title: Where a class's practice is read
handbook.what: Telling the two pages of a class apart. The class page carries what the class has practised together, its minutes in the app and how far it has travelled. This page is the class's tools: the roster, the teachers, the join link, renaming and deleting.
handbook.where: The line under the class name at the top of the tools page.
how: Read the line.
Tap **Open the class page** to go to the class's practice.
handbook.note: Nothing on this page totals whole-class play. A class played from the front shows its minutes on the class page, never here.

handbook.title: Where classes are in the course and where they stop
handbook.what: Where in the course your classes have got to, shown as the last phrase each class played, and the point most of them stop before. An organisation with no classes does not see this question.
handbook.where: The **Journey** question on any level's insights page, under Quiet.
how: Read the sentence for how many classes have started, how far the furthest have got and where most stop.
Read the funnel: each step is a sentence of the course, and the bar is how many classes have reached it.
Read the class rows, furthest first, for each class's own position.
handbook.note: A position is the phrase the class last played, in both languages. A sentence is one of the course's own sentences; the count out of the total says how far along that is.

handbook.title: Where in the world people are using us, and on what
handbook.what: Which countries real people practised from in the last thirty days, whether they were on phones, tablets or desktops, and whether they were in the app or in a browser.
handbook.where: **Where and what**, under What's happening.
how: Read the sentence for how many real people, from how many countries, and the country and device most of them are on.
Read the chart for people by country, most first.

Read the rows, one per country, each with its phone, tablet and desktop split and its in-the-app or in-a-browser split. Tap a country to narrow the page to it; tap a device chip to count only that device. Both choices are written into the page address.
handbook.note: A person seen on two devices is counted once in the headline and once under each device. In the app or in a browser has only been recorded since 10 September 2026, so earlier people read as not recorded rather than being guessed at. Machine traffic is left out by rule.

handbook.title: Where the class has got to
handbook.what: How far the class has travelled through its course, as a bar in phrases with the next belt named. A class is one learner account played from the front, so this is the class's own place on the course, moved by the sessions you run together.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Course Journey** card in the column beside the roster.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Read the bar for how much of the course the class has covered.
Read the line under it for how far it is to the next belt.
handbook.note: A class that has never played says **Not started** in words; it is never shown as a bar of zero.

handbook.title: Whether a class is practising together
handbook.what: The headline card on a class: how many phrases the class was prompted with together in the last seven days, when it last practised, and the list of those phrases with how often each came round. Classes practising together is what a language programme lives on, so this leads over anything individual students do alone.
handbook.where: The **Class practice** card on a class page.
how: Open a class from the tree or the map.
Read the big figure for phrases practised this week.
The line under it gives the time since the class last practised and its minutes in the app this week.
The list beneath is the three phrases the class practised most this week and the number of times each came round; **Show all** under it opens the whole list.
handbook.note: The minutes are time in the app with the lesson running, pauses included, so they are the time the class was in the lesson. A class that has never played together says so plainly and names the teacher's **Play as class** button as the thing that starts the first lesson.

handbook.title: Whether the app is working right now
handbook.what: Whether audio is failing for real people, and on which build and which kind of device, so you can tell if the last fix reached them.
handbook.where: **Working now**, under What's happening.
how: Read the sentence for the failure rate over the last seven days and the build most people are on today.
Read the chart for the rate by day.
Read the rows, one per build, most people first. Tap a build to narrow the rows to it; the choice is written into the page address.
Read the device line under the rows for phones against desktops.
handbook.note: Only real people's plays are counted, so your own session on staging is not here. Machine traffic is left out by rule.

handbook.title: Which bits of a course make people stumble
handbook.what: Seeing, for one course, which pieces of it real learners skip, retry, or stop on, ranked by how much trouble each piece caused per person who met it.
handbook.where: **Weak points**, under What's happening. Pick a course on the left.
how: Tap a course under **Courses** in the map on the left.
Read the sentence for the piece that gave people the most trouble.
Read the rows, worst first, showing both languages for each piece.
Open a row to see that piece's phrases.
handbook.note: When fewer than five real people have practised a course, the page says **too few to say** rather than showing a number. That is the truth about the course, not a fault in the page.

handbook.title: Which classes have gone quiet
handbook.what: The half you act on: which classes practised before and have stopped, how long ago, and which have never started at all. An organisation with no classes does not see this question.
handbook.where: The **Quiet** question on any level's insights page, under Practising.
how: Read the sentence for how many classes have gone quiet and how many have never started.
Read the bars for how long since each class last practised.
Open a class row to see where it stopped.
handbook.note: Practised this week counts any sign of practice, a phrase reached in a lesson or the course opened and progress saved. The Practising figure above counts phrases practised only, so it can be lower.

handbook.title: Which classes practised this week
handbook.what: Whether your classes are actually doing it: how many practised together in the last seven days against the seven before, how many phrases they practised, and which people practised on their own account and for how long. An organisation with no classes reads only the people line here, asked as how many of your people practised.
handbook.where: The **Practising** question at the top of any level's insights page.
how: Read the sentence for this week against last week.
Read the line for how many phrases were practised each day over the last four weeks.
Read the class rows for who practised, when they last practised together and where in the course they are.
Read the people rows for own-account minutes.
handbook.note: A class's minutes are time in the app on its own class account, the gaps between phrases included, the same number its class page shows. People's minutes are their own logins.

handbook.title: Which courses are worth attention
handbook.what: One ranking of every course by real people practising it this month, with how many have ever been in it and how many have reached its end.
handbook.where: **Courses**, under What's happening.
how: Read the sentence for how many courses are alive this month and which had the most people.
Read the chart for the courses with anybody in them, most first.
Use the chips to show every course, only the alive ones, or the quiet ones somebody once joined. The chip is written into the page address.
Open a course row to see which bits of it people stumble on.
handbook.note: Reaching the end means getting through nine tenths of the course. A course with no recorded length shows a dash there rather than a zero. Minutes are not shown: the stored counters are not reliable, and a number that might be wrong is left off.

handbook.title: Who is about to leave
handbook.what: The list of who to write to and why: real people who were practising regularly and have stopped, paying people who have gone quiet, and people whose access runs out within a fortnight.
handbook.where: **Leaving**, under What's happening.
how: Read the sentence for how many, and why.
Read the chart for how long they have been gone.
Read the rows, most recently seen first, then the most regular first. Each carries every reason that applies.
Open a row to see that person and act on them.
handbook.note: Nobody is ranked by money. No amount is stored anywhere in this database, so the order is who was seen most recently and who was most regular before they stopped. This page sends nothing.

handbook.title: Who is behind every number
handbook.what: Saying, under every answer, how many real people the numbers on that page are counted from and who has been left out. Demo accounts, SSi staff, class accounts and machine traffic are never counted as people.
handbook.where: The small pill beneath the answer sentence on every question page.
how: Read the pill under the answer for the number of real people counted.
If a page is deliberately showing demo or staff data, the pill says so in red.
handbook.note: The count comes from the server, from one shared rule, never from the page itself. Two pages cannot disagree about who is real.

handbook.title: Why the insights show a rate, not a total
handbook.what: Everything on the insights page is a rate — an amount per learner per week — rather than a running total. A total only ever says how big and how old something is, so a large school always beats a small one. A rate says how fast it is moving, which is the thing you can actually act on.
handbook.where: The comparison block under the pickers on any level's insights page.
how: Open a level and tap **See insights**.
Read the line under the pickers — it says in words what the current measure counts.
The block below puts this level's rate beside whatever you are comparing it to.
Change the window to compute the same rate over a shorter or longer period.
handbook.note: A pace matters more than a position: a class three sentences behind but climbing fast is healthier than one parked far ahead.

handbook.title: Work through setup at your own pace
handbook.what: The first-run wizard that takes a brand-new school from nothing to teachers, courses and classes. It is four short steps and it does not have to be done in one sitting.
handbook.where: Settings, then First-time setup. The steps are listed down the left, and **Save & exit** sits at the bottom of every one.
how: Open the wizard and work down the steps on the left — your school, your staff, your courses, your classes.
**Continue** saves the step you are on and moves you to the next one.
Tap any step in the left-hand list to jump straight to it, forwards or back.
**Save & exit** saves the step you are on and puts you back on your dashboard. If something cannot be saved it stays put and tells you why, so you never leave work behind without knowing.
Come back to Settings and First-time setup whenever you want to carry on.
handbook.note: Nothing here is a one-shot. Everything the wizard sets up — the school name, the invite links, the classes — can also be changed later from Settings and from your class pages. The course ticks on step three are only a filter for the class list on step four, so they are not kept when you leave.

handbook.title: Your class against the average
handbook.what: The teacher's own insight tool: pick one of your classes and see its pace set against the average, over the period and for the measure you choose. It answers whether a class is moving well, which a roster of totals cannot.
handbook.where: **Analytics** in the schools navigation.
how: Open **Analytics**.
Pick the class you want from **Your classes** if you teach more than one.
Pick the **measure** — the line underneath says exactly what it counts.
Pick the **window** the rate is computed over, and what to **compare to**.
Read the comparison block for your class's rate beside that average.
handbook.note: A class with too few sessions to compare honestly says so rather than showing a number built from nothing.

handbook.title: Your classes at a glance
handbook.what: Your teaching dashboard, with your classes first. Every class you teach is a row or a card carrying its course, the minutes it spent in the app this week, the phrases it practised, how far it has travelled through the course, when it last played, and the join code you read out to get a new pupil in. The minutes are the class's own, from the lessons you ran with Play as class. Beside them, kept apart and never added in, is what the pupils did on their own accounts this week, said in words when there is nothing.
handbook.where: The schools dashboard you land on, above everything else on the page.
how: Open the schools dashboard.
Read down the list — one entry per class you teach.
Tap a class name to open its class page, with what it practised this week and how far it has got.
**Play as class** on any entry starts a session the whole class does together, on the class's own account.
handbook.note: A class that has never played says **Not started** in words. A brand new account shows a single button to create your first class instead of the list.

handbook.title: Your own teaching numbers
handbook.what: One quiet line totalling your classes this week: how many classes, the minutes they spent in the app with a lesson running, and the phrases they practised. All of it is the classes' own play from the front. A second line, always there, is the minutes your pupils spent on their own accounts this week, kept apart from the first and never added to it. When no pupil has practised on their own account it says so in words, because that is usual for a class taught from the front and not a fault.
handbook.where: Underneath your classes on the schools dashboard.
how: Open the schools dashboard and scroll past your classes.
**Classes** is how many you teach.
**In the app this week** is time with a lesson running, pauses included.
**Phrases practised** is how many phrases your classes were prompted with this week.
handbook.note: The line only appears once you have at least one class.
